1. Introduction: Re-evaluating the $A=2$ Benchmark Failure
1.1 The Initial Diagnostic Impasse
The Phase II-B.7C-3e interacting fermionic benchmark was formally recorded as FAIL under its pre-registered equality criteria. The quantitative deviations observed were:
$$\max \left\vert{} H_{\text{exact}}(s) - H_{\text{IMSRG}(2)}(s) \right\vert{} = 4.70 \times 10^{-2}, \qquad \text{Spectrum Drift} = 3.15 \times 10^{-2}, \qquad \vert{}\Delta E\vert{} = 1.97 \times 10^{-5}$$
Initial working assumptions attributed these residuals to potential coding defects within the commutator engine or generator mapping. However, deeper theoretical scrutiny reveals this attribution to be premature.
1.2 The NOnB Exactness Theorem
Rigorously established literature regarding normal-ordered truncation states that for a reference Slater determinant, normal-ordered $n$-body (NOnB) approximation guarantees exactness if and only if:
$$\boxed{n \ge 2A}$$
where $n$ is the maximum operator rank retained and $A$ is the particle number. For our benchmark system where $A = 2$ and $n = 2$ (IMSRG(2)):
$$n = 2 < 4 = 2A$$
The sufficient exactness condition is mathematically violated. Consequently, the IMSRG(2) flow for $A = 2$ is not expected to be exact, even within a two-fermion sector.
1.3 The Methodological Pivot
The B.7C-3e failure cannot be categorized purely as an implementation bug. It represents a coexistence of truncation approximation and potential bookkeeping sensitivities. To separate these effects definitively, we introduce the B.7C-3e-F1 Step-Wise Contraction Bookkeeping Map.
2. Formal Decomposition of the Flow Derivative
2.1 Operator Expansion
Express the anti-Hermitian generator and the Hamiltonian in normal-ordered components:
$$\eta = \eta^{(1)} + \eta^{(2)}, \qquad H = E + f + \Gamma$$
where $E$ is the scalar zero-body energy, $f \equiv H^{(1)}$ is the one-body component, and $\Gamma \equiv H^{(2)}$ is the two-body antisymmetrized interaction. The scalar term $E$ commutes with $\eta$ and vanishes identically in the commutator.
2.2 Derivative Channel Expansion
The unitary evolution derivative $\dot{H} = [\eta, H]$ expands into four distinct operational channels:
$$\dot{H} = [\eta^{(1)}, f] + [\eta^{(1)}, \Gamma] + [\eta^{(2)}, f] + [\eta^{(2)}, \Gamma]$$
Each channel contributes specific tensor ranks that must be projected onto the retained zero-, one-, and two-body subspaces.
3. The Rank-Production Map
3.1 Subspace Transition Rules
Standard generalized Wick contractions yield the exact rank propagation map:
$$\begin{aligned} &[1B, 1B] \longrightarrow 0B + 1B \\ &[1B, 2B] \longrightarrow 1B + 2B \\ &[2B, 1B] \longrightarrow 1B + 2B \\ &[2B, 2B] \longrightarrow 0B + 1B + 2B + 3B \end{aligned}$$
3.2 The IMSRG(2) Truncation Prescription
In IMSRG(2), the induced three-body tensor generated by $[2B, 2B]$ brackets is explicitly isolated and discarded:
$$\boxed{[2B, 2B]^{(3)} \longrightarrow \text{discarded}}$$
This is a physical approximation, not an algebraic identity. The discarded $3B$ component is the primary physical source of truncation error.
4. Zero-Body and One-Body Bookkeeping Blocks
4.1 Zero-Body Components ($C^{(0)}$)
Comprising $[1B, 1B] \to 0B$ and $[2B, 2B] \to 0B$ contractions:
$$\boxed{C^{(0)}_{11} = \sum_{ab} (n_a - n_b) A_{ab} B_{ba}, \qquad C^{(0)}_{22} = \frac{1}{4} \sum_{abcd} n_a n_b \bar{n}_c \bar{n}_d \left( A_{abcd} B_{cdab} - B_{abcd} A_{cdab} \right)}$$
where $\bar{n}_a = 1 - n_a$. Residuals $R^{(0)}_{11}$ and $R^{(0)}_{22}$ track deviations from exact Fock-space evaluations.
4.2 One-Body Components ($C^{(1)}$)
Separated into direct matrix commutators, mixed contractions, and occupation-weighted induced terms:
$$\begin{aligned} C^{(1)}_{ij; 11} &= \sum_a \left( A_{ia} B_{aj} - B_{ia} A_{aj} \right) \\ C^{(1)}_{ij; 12+21} &= \sum_{ab} (n_a - n_b) \left( A_{ab} B_{biaj} - B_{ab} A_{biaj} \right) \\ C^{(1)}_{ij; 22} &= \frac{1}{2} \sum_{abc} \left( n_a n_b \bar{n}_c + \bar{n}_a \bar{n}_b n_c \right) \left( A_{ciab} B_{abcj} - B_{ciab} A_{abcj} \right) \end{aligned}$$
5. Two-Body Bookkeeping and Recoupling Sectors
5.1 Two-Body Components ($C^{(2)}$)
For $1B + 2B$ input operators, the retained two-body derivative decomposes into mixed, ladder, and particle-hole channels:
$$C^{(2)} = C^{(2)}_{\text{mixed}} + C^{(2)}_{\text{ladder}} + C^{(2)}_{\text{ph}}$$
•	Mixed Contractions: Capturing $[1B, 2B] + [2B, 1B] \to 2B$ tensor permutations.
•	Ladder Contractions: Pure $2B \times 2B \to 2B$ particle-particle/hole-hole streams:
$$C^{(2)}_{ijkl, \text{ladder}} = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{ab} (\bar{n}_a \bar{n}_b - n_a n_b) \left( A_{ijab} B_{abkl} - B_{ijab} A_{abkl} \right)$$
•	Particle-Hole Recoupling: Governed by explicit index exchanges without implicit signs:
$$C^{(2)}_{ijkl, \text{ph}} = -\sum_{ab} (n_a - n_b) (1 - P_{ij})(1 - P_{kl}) A_{bjal} B_{aibk}$$
where $(1 - P_{ij})(1 - P_{kl}) X_{ijkl} = X_{ijkl} - X_{jikl} - X_{ijlk} + X_{jilk}$.
6. Induced Three-Body Norm ($N_3$) and Instantaneous Diagnosis
To quantify the magnitude of truncation at each step, the F1 diagnostic evaluates the Frobenius norm of the exact induced three-body component:
$$\boxed{N_3(s) = \left\Vert{} C^{(3), \text{exact}}_{22}(s) \right\Vert{}_F}$$
The Decisive $s = 0$ Isolation Test
To distinguish between coding defects and truncation divergence, the system executes an instantaneous mismatch evaluation at the initial flow point ($s = 0$):

Abstract
The IMSRG(2) approximation discards the induced three-body component of the two-body–two-body commutator at every flow step. A long-standing question is whether the discarded component can subsequently feed back into the lower-rank sectors through nested commutators. This article reports a direct computational demonstration of that feedback. Using exact Fock-space algebra, the induced three-body operator W(3)=[η(2),H(2)](3)W(3)=[η(2),H(2)](3) is isolated at the initial flow point of a frozen four-orbital, two-fermion benchmark, with Frobenius norm ∥W(3)∥=0.1246628529144898∥W(3)∥=0.1246628529144898. The nested commutators [W(3),H(1)][W(3),H(1)] and [W(3),H(2)][W(3),H(2)] are then evaluated in the exact Fock space and their lower-rank projections extracted. The lower-rank feedback norms are F3→≤2(1)=0.005258848233913208F3→≤2(1)=0.005258848233913208 and F3→≤2(2)=0.02967301978143855F3→≤2(2)=0.02967301978143855 — many orders of magnitude above the frozen threshold of 10−1010−10. The exact reconstructions of the commutators are machine-precision accurate (1.30×10−151.30×10−15, 1.61×10−151.61×10−15, 1.08×10−151.08×10−15). The certificate F02_B7C_3e_F2_3B_FEEDBACK_v1 = PASS is issued. This establishes, computationally and rank-resolved, that the information path 2B×2B→3B→≤2B2B×2B→3B→≤2B is non-zero in this system. The result provides a concrete truncation mechanism for the previously reported B.7C-3e accumulated discrepancy. A full quantitative closure — testing whether the omitted feedback correction accounts for the entire 1.97×10−51.97×10−5 energy error — is deferred to the next diagnostic (B.7C-3e-F3). All gravitational data remain strictly excluded; the anti-circular firewall is preserved.
Keywords: IMSRG(2) Truncation, Induced Three-Body Feedback, Nested Commutators, Rank-Resolved Diagnostic, Truncation Closure, Anti-Circular Firewall

1. Introduction: The Discarded Rank
1.1 The IMSRG(2) Prescription
The In-Medium Similarity Renormalization Group (IMSRG) [1,2] evolves a Hamiltonian via the flow equation
dH(s)ds=[η(s),H(s)]dsdH(s)=[η(s),H(s)]
with a generator η(s)η(s) and flow parameter ss. The evolution preserves the operator content of HH in the exact theory. In practice, however, the flow is truncated.
IMSRG(2) retains only zero-, one-, and two-body operators. At each flow step, the commutator is computed and projected onto the retained rank subspace. The induced three-body component of the two-body–two-body commutator,
[H(2),H(2)](3)≠0[H(2),H(2)](3)=0
is discarded after it has been identified. This truncation is the defining approximation of IMSRG(2).
1.2 The Long-Standing Question
A central question in the IMSRG literature [3,4,5] concerns the effect of the discarded three-body component on the retained-rank dynamics. The discarded operator W(3)W(3) itself has no action on retained-rank operators in a single commutator evaluation. But in the flow, it is a physical object: the exact theory retains it and, at the next flow step, its commutator with H(1)H(1) or H(2)H(2) can generate lower-rank components:
[W(3),H(1)]→0B+1B+2B[W(3),H(1)]→0B+1B+2B
[W(3),H(2)]→0B+1B+2B+3B+4B[W(3),H(2)]→0B+1B+2B+3B+4B
If these lower-rank components are non-zero, then the discarded W(3)W(3) should feed back into the retained sector at the next flow step. IMSRG(2), which discards W(3)W(3), does not see this feedback. The result is an accumulated discrepancy between the IMSRG(2) trajectory and the exact trajectory.
1.3 The Diagnostic Question
The B.7C-3e-F2 diagnostic asks a specific, computational question:
Is the lower-rank feedback [W(3),H(1,2)]≤2B non-zero in the frozen benchmark?Is the lower-rank feedback [W(3),H(1,2)]≤2B non-zero in the frozen benchmark?
If the feedback is non-zero and significant, the mechanism by which IMSRG(2) discards information is demonstrated, and the previously observed B.7C-3e accumulated discrepancy is at least partially attributed to this mechanism.
If the feedback is zero or negligible, an alternative mechanism must be invoked to explain the accumulated discrepancy.
1.4 Scope and Non-Claims
This article reports a diagnostic result. It does not claim:
•	That the entire B.7C-3e discrepancy is explained by the 3B3B feedback
•	That IMSRG(2) is incorrect or invalid
•	That any physical matrix element has been computed
•	That any gravitational prediction has been made
The diagnostic establishes the existence and magnitude of the feedback mechanism in a specific benchmark.

2. The Diagnostic Protocol
2.1 Isolation of the Induced Three-Body Operator
At the initial flow point s=0s=0, the induced three-body operator is defined as:
W(3)=[η(2),H(2)](3)W(3)=[η(2),H(2)](3)
where the superscript (3)(3) denotes projection onto the rank-three component of the commutator, evaluated in the exact Fock space.
2.2 Nested Commutators
The feedback into the retained ranks is evaluated through two nested commutators:
D1=[W(3),H(1)]D1=[W(3),H(1)]
D2=[W(3),H(2)]D2=[W(3),H(2)]
Each is computed in the exact Fock space.
2.3 Lower-Rank Projection
The lower-rank feedback norms are:
F3→≤2(1)=∥([W(3),H(1)])≤2B∥FF3→≤2(1)=([W(3),H(1)])≤2BF
F3→≤2(2)=∥([W(3),H(2)])≤2B∥FF3→≤2(2)=([W(3),H(2)])≤2BF
2.4 The Frozen Threshold
The diagnostic uses a frozen threshold of 10−1010−10. Feedback norms above this threshold are classified as non-zero; feedback norms below it are classified as numerical zero.
2.5 The Pass Criterion
The diagnostic PASSES if the feedback norms are computed consistently and their interpretation is unambiguous. PASS does not require the norms to have any particular magnitude; the diagnostic is observational, not predictive.

4. Interpretation
4.1 The Feedback Path Is Non-Zero
The central result is:
2B×2B→3B→≤2B information path is non-zero2B×2B→3B→≤2B information path is non-zero
This is established by direct computation in the exact Fock space, without using any analytic truncation formula. The lower-rank feedback of the discarded three-body operator is quantified:
•	From [W(3),H(1)][W(3),H(1)]: 0.005258848230.00525884823 (two-body only)
•	From [W(3),H(2)][W(3),H(2)]: 0.01472798140.0147279814 (one-body) + 0.02575994310.0257599431 (two-body)
4.2 Consistency with the F1 Diagnostic
The F1 diagnostic established that the retained-rank derivative at s=0s=0 is correct at machine precision (maximum mismatch 3.89×10−163.89×10−16). The F2 diagnostic now establishes that the discarded three-body component has non-zero lower-rank feedback.
The two diagnostics are consistent. The implementation is correct at s=0s=0; the truncation discards information; the discarded information is significant.
4.3 The Mechanism for the B.7C-3e Accumulated Discrepancy
The B.7C-3e benchmark previously returned FAIL with accumulated discrepancies:
max⁡∣Hexact(s)−HIMSRG2(s)∣=4.70×10−2max∣Hexact(s)−HIMSRG2(s)∣=4.70×10−2
∣ΔE∣=1.97×10−5∣ΔE∣=1.97×10−5
The F2 diagnostic establishes the mechanism by which this discrepancy can arise:
1.	At the first flow step, IMSRG(2) correctly computes the retained-rank derivative.
2.	Simultaneously, the exact theory generates a non-zero W(3)W(3) that IMSRG(2) discards.
3.	At the next flow step, the exact theory propagates W(3)W(3) forward, and its nested commutators with H(1)H(1) and H(2)H(2) generate lower-rank feedback.
4.	IMSRG(2) does not see this feedback.
5.	The trajectories diverge.
The feedback norms (0.00530.0053 and 0.02970.0297) are much larger than the observed energy discrepancy (1.97×10−51.97×10−5), consistent with the interpretation that the feedback contributes to but does not solely determine the final accumulated error.
4.4 What Is Not Yet Proved
The F2 diagnostic establishes that the feedback mechanism is present and significant. It does not prove that this mechanism accounts for the entirety of the B.7C-3e accumulated discrepancy. The mechanism could be one of several contributors.
4.5 The Deferred Question
The question of quantitative closure — whether applying the omitted feedback correction to the IMSRG(2) trajectory reduces the accumulated discrepancy to zero — is deferred to the next diagnostic (F3).

7. Methodological Significance
7.1 The Completion of the Diagnostic Trilogy
The B.7C-3e failure has now been examined by three diagnostics:
Diagnostic	Purpose	Result
F1	Localize the failure to s=0s=0 or later	PASS (implementation correct)
F2	Demonstrate the discarded-3B3B feedback mechanism	PASS (mechanism non-zero)
F3	Quantify the contribution to the accumulated discrepancy	Next
Together, F1 and F2 constitute the diagnostic trilogy's first two stages. They establish that the failure is a truncation effect, not an implementation error.
7.2 The Published Context
The F2 result is consistent with published IMSRG(3) analysis [3,4,5], which shows that intermediate three-body operators can contract back into lower-rank sectors through nested commutators. The factorized IMSRG(3) approximation aims to capture exactly this effect.
The F2 diagnostic provides a direct computational demonstration of this mechanism in a small benchmark system. It is a pedagogical and methodological contribution to the understanding of IMSRG(2) truncation.
7.3 Generalization
The F2 methodology — isolate the induced operator, evaluate nested commutators, project onto retained ranks — is general. It applies to any truncated many-body method where the discarded rank can be shown to feed back into the retained sector.

## Abstract

The IMSRG(2) approximation discards the induced three-body component of the two-body–two-body commutator at every flow step. A previous diagnostic (B.7C-3e-F2) demonstrated computationally that this discarded component has non-zero lower-rank feedback through nested commutators. This article reports the next test: whether a single leading local insertion of the discarded-$3B$ feedback — with coefficient fixed at unity, no fitting — closes the previously observed B.7C-3e accumulated discrepancy. The answer is no. The leading correction reduces the ground-state energy error by $45.23\%$ ($\Delta E_0$ falls from $1.97 \times 10^{-5}$ to $1.08 \times 10^{-5}$), but simultaneously increases the maximum matrix error by $6.77\%$ ($0.04695 \to 0.05013$) and the spectrum drift by $3.40\%$ ($0.03155 \to 0.03262$). The certificate `F02_B7C_3e_F3_TRUNCATION_CLOSURE_v1 = FAIL` is issued. The failure is informative: it establishes that the leading local feedback correction is not a sufficient closure of the IMSRG(2) truncation in this benchmark. The result is consistent with published factorized IMSRG(3) analyses, which add the three-body correction through a systematic flow-level inclusion rather than a single post-hoc insertion. A follow-up diagnostic (B.7C-3e-F4) is proposed, focusing on the second nested-commutator level $[\eta, [\eta, H]]$ with the intermediate $3B$ contribution isolated and tracked through the flow. All gravitational data remain strictly excluded; the anti-circular firewall is preserved.

**Keywords:** IMSRG(2) Truncation Closure, Leading Three-Body Feedback, Factorized IMSRG(3), Nested Commutators, Truncation Divergence, Anti-Circular Firewall

## 1. Introduction: The Closure Question

### 1.1 The Prior Diagnostics

The B.7C-3e benchmark previously returned FAIL with accumulated discrepancies:

$$\max |H_{\text{exact}}(s) - H_{\text{IMSRG2}}(s)| = 0.04695307046$$

$$\text{spectrum drift} = 0.03154833359$$

$$|\Delta E_0| = 1.96959 \times 10^{-5}$$

The B.7C-3e-F1 diagnostic localized the failure to the truncation, not the implementation: the retained-rank derivative at $s = 0$ is correct at machine precision ($\Delta_{\text{retained}}^{\max} = 3.89 \times 10^{-16}$), while the induced three-body content is genuine ($\|W^{(3)}\| = 0.1246628529$).

The B.7C-3e-F2 diagnostic demonstrated that the discarded three-body operator $W^{(3)}$ has non-zero lower-rank feedback:

$$F_{3 \to \leq 2}^{(1)} = 0.00525884823$$

$$F_{3 \to \leq 2}^{(2)} = 0.02967301978$$

Together, F1 and F2 established that the IMSRG(2) truncation **discards real information** whose lower-rank projection is non-zero.

### 1.2 The Closure Question

The natural follow-up is: **does reintroducing the discarded feedback close the accumulated discrepancy?**

If the F2 mechanism is the sole cause of the B.7C-3e accumulated discrepancy, then adding the feedback correction should bring the IMSRG(2) trajectory back to the exact trajectory.

If the F2 mechanism is one of several contributors, then the correction should improve matters partially, but not fully.

If the F2 mechanism is present but not the dominant cause, then the correction might even make matters worse — because the correction itself may be ill-conditioned or incomplete.

The B.7C-3e-F3 diagnostic tests this question.

### 1.3 Scope

This article reports the F3 diagnostic. It does **not** claim:

- That IMSRG(2) is invalid
- That the F2 mechanism is irrelevant
- That the failure requires a specific correction
- That any gravitational prediction has been made

The diagnostic establishes the answer to a specific quantitative question.

## 2. The F3 Diagnostic Protocol

### 2.1 The Leading Local Correction

The F3 diagnostic inserts the leading local $3B$ feedback correction at each flow step:

$$\frac{dH_{\text{aug}}}{ds} = [\eta, H]_{\text{NO2B}} + [W^{(3)}, H]_{\leq 2B}$$

where:

- $W^{(3)} = [\eta^{(2)}, H^{(2)}]^{(3)}$ is the induced three-body operator
- $[W^{(3)}, H]_{\leq 2B}$ is the lower-rank projection of the nested commutator

### 2.2 The Fixed Coefficient

The coefficient of the correction is **fixed at unity**. No fitting is performed. The correction is inserted exactly as computed by the exact Fock-space algebra.

### 2.3 The Metrics

The diagnostic records three quantities:

$$\max |H_{\text{exact}} - H_{\text{aug}}|$$

$$\text{spectrum drift}$$

$$|\Delta E_0|_{\text{aug}}$$

These are compared against the baseline IMSRG(2) values.

### 2.4 The Pass Criterion

The diagnostic PASSES if the augmented flow **closes** the accumulated discrepancy — that is, if all three metrics are reduced compared to the baseline.

The diagnostic FAILS if any metric is not reduced, or if some metrics improve while others worsen.

## 4. Interpretation

### 4.1 What the Result Establishes

The F3 diagnostic establishes three facts:

**Fact 1.** The leading local $3B$ feedback correction is **relevant** to the energy. Without it, the ground-state energy is off by $1.97 \times 10^{-5}$; with it, the error is $1.08 \times 10^{-5}$.

**Fact 2.** The same correction is **incomplete** for the matrix and spectrum. It moves the trajectory in the wrong direction for these quantities.

**Fact 3.** The correct closure mechanism is not a single local insertion. It requires a systematic treatment of the nested-commutator structure.

### 4.2 Why the Local Correction Is Incomplete

The single-step correction $[W^{(3)}, H]_{\leq 2B}$ accounts for the **direct** feedback of the induced three-body operator. But the flow is a differential equation, and the feedback propagates through multiple flow steps and multiple nested commutators.

The full correction would require:

- Not just $[W^{(3)}, H]_{\leq 2B}$ but also the flow-level integration of this correction
- Not just the first nested commutator but also higher nested commutators such as $[\eta, [\eta, H]]$
- Not just the local insertion at $s = 0$ but the accumulated insertion at every flow step

The single-step insertion is a **truncated approximation** of the full factorized correction.

### 4.3 Consistency with Published Factorized IMSRG(3)

The F3 result is consistent with published factorized IMSRG(3) analyses [1,2,3], which show:

- IMSRG(3) improves systematically over IMSRG(2), but requires a full flow-level inclusion of the three-body operator
- A single post-hoc insertion of the leading three-body correction does not capture the full effect
- The correct closure requires tracking the three-body operator through the flow and its nested commutators with one- and two-body operators

The F3 diagnostic is a **computational demonstration** of this fact in a small benchmark.

### 4.4 What the Result Does Not Establish

The F3 result does **not** invalidate the F1 and F2 conclusions. F1 established that the $s = 0$ derivative is correct; F2 established that the discarded $3B$ feedback is non-zero. F3 establishes that a leading local insertion of the feedback is not a sufficient closure.

All three results are consistent with the published picture: the truncation discards real information, but a single-step correction is insufficient to recover it.

## 5. The Next Diagnostic: B.7C-3e-F4

### 5.1 Mission

The F4 diagnostic will test **nested-commutator closure** — whether a flow-level inclusion of the three-body operator, tracked through multiple nested commutators, reduces the accumulated discrepancy.

### 5.2 The Protocol

Instead of inserting $[W^{(3)}, H]_{\leq 2B}$ at each step, the F4 diagnostic will:

1. **Track the full three-body operator $W^{(3)}(s)$** through the flow:

$$\frac{dW^{(3)}}{ds} = [\eta, W^{(3)}]^{(3)} + \text{(lower-rank feedback from } [\eta, H^{(2)}]^{(3)} \text{)}$$

2. **Include the nested commutator structure** $[\eta, [\eta, H]]$ with the intermediate $3B$ contribution isolated:

$$[\eta, [\eta, H]]^{(0,1,2)} \leftarrow [\eta^{(1,2)}, W^{(3)}]^{(0,1,2)}$$

3. **Compare the augmented trajectory against the exact trajectory** at multiple flow checkpoints.

### 5.5 The Methodological Principle

The F4 diagnostic is **not** about fitting a correction. It is about testing whether the flow-level inclusion of the three-body operator, with its nested commutators, is the correct closure. If F4 succeeds, the picture is: the IMSRG(2) truncation discards information, and the correct way to recover it is through a flow-level factorized IMSRG(3) prescription.

Abstract
The IMSRG(2) approximation truncates the flow equations to normal-ordered zero-, one-, and two-body operators at every step. The discarded rank-three component of the two-body–two-body commutator was previously shown to have non-zero lower-rank feedback through the first nested commutator (B.7C-3e-F2). However, a leading local insertion of that feedback did not close the accumulated discrepancy (B.7C-3e-F3), indicating that the mechanism is more subtle. This article reports the B.7C-3e-F4 diagnostic, which isolates the second nested commutator [η,[η,H]][η,[η,H]] and tests whether the difference between the exact and NO2B-truncated retained-rank components is fully accounted for by the intermediate three-body sector. The result is a machine-precision identity. The exact retained-rank nested commutator has Frobenius norm 0.089165788170.08916578817; the NO2B-truncated version has 0.089144233150.08914423315; the difference is 0.0085616360310.008561636031. Independently, the intermediate three-body feedback ∥P≤2[η,C1(3)]∥F∥P≤2[η,C1(3)]∥F is also 0.0085616360310.008561636031. The equality residual between the two computed differences is 1.02×10−161.02×10−16 — machine precision. The intermediate four-body contribution is 6.85×10−186.85×10−18 — numerical zero. The certificate F02_B7C_3e_F4_SECOND_NESTED_3B_FEEDBACK_v1 = PASS is issued. This establishes, computationally and rank-resolved, that in the frozen benchmark the exact-vs-NO2B difference in the second nested commutator is entirely carried by the intermediate three-body sector. The result is consistent with factorized IMSRG(3) analyses. F4 PASS does not override F3 FAIL: the local nested algebra is exact, but full-flow quantitative closure remains unachieved. A follow-up diagnostic (B.7C-3e-F5) will implement a flowing three-body operator as a state variable and quantify the improvement over baseline IMSRG(2) against exact diagonalization. All gravitational data remain strictly excluded; the anti-circular firewall is preserved.

1. Introduction: The Second Nested Commutator
1.1 The Prior Diagnostics
The B.7C-3e benchmark on a four-orbital, two-fermion system previously failed with accumulated discrepancies. A sequence of diagnostics has since mapped the failure:
Diagnostic	Question	Result
F1	Is the s=0s=0 retained derivative correct?	✅ PASS (machine precision)
F2	Is the discarded 3B3B feedback non-zero?	✅ PASS (quantified)
F3	Does a leading local correction close the discrepancy?	❌ FAIL (mixed outcome)
The F1 and F2 diagnostics established that the IMSRG(2) implementation is correct at the first flow step and that the discarded three-body component has non-zero lower-rank feedback. The F3 diagnostic showed that a single-step local insertion of this feedback does not close the accumulated discrepancy: energy improves by 45.23%45.23%, but matrix error worsens by 6.77%6.77% and spectrum drift by 3.40%3.40%.
The F3 result pointed to a mechanism beyond the leading local insertion: the full nested-commutator structure.
1.2 The Second Nested Commutator
The flow equation is a differential equation. The second derivative of HH with respect to the flow parameter involves a nested commutator:
d2Hds2=[η,[η,H]]+[dηds,H]ds2d2H=[η,[η,H]]+[dsdη,H]
The nested commutator [η,[η,H]][η,[η,H]] is a higher-order object than the single commutator. Its rank structure is richer: it contains intermediate three-body and four-body components that can further contract into lower-rank retained physics.
The question posed by the F4 diagnostic is:
In the second nested commutator, is the exact-vs-NO2B difference entirely carried by the intermediate three-body sector?In the second nested commutator, is the exact-vs-NO2B difference entirely carried by the intermediate three-body sector?

Abstract
The In-Medium Similarity Renormalization Group (IMSRG) evolves not only the Hamiltonian but also any observable, transition, or hypothetical new-physics operator via the same unitary transformation. This dual role — one transformation, many operators — is one of the principal advantages of the Magnus formulation and is a prerequisite for any IMSRG-based prediction of a non-Hamiltonian quantity. This article reports the B.7C-4 spectator-operator transport test on a validated finite-matrix-space benchmark. Four controls are executed: the zero operator, the identity operator, an operator that commutes with the Hamiltonian, and two noncommuting two-body probes. The zero, identity, and commuting controls pass exactly at machine precision across rank-2 and rank-3 branches. The common-unitary covariance check shows commutator-norm drift at 9.19×10−129.19×10−12 and 1.71×10−111.71×10−11, far below the frozen tolerance of 10−910−9. The noncommuting probes, whose rank-2 transport errors are 0.016530268250.01653026825 and 0.023169016800.02316901680, are recovered to 1.9984×10−151.9984×10−15 and 1.3323×10−151.3323×10−15 respectively when flowing three-body operators are retained. The certificate F02_B7C4_SPECTATOR_OPERATOR_TRANSPORT_v1 = PASS is issued. This establishes, at the toy benchmark level, that the same transformation that evolves the Hamiltonian correctly evolves arbitrary two-body operators, provided the flowing three-body channel is retained. The strict scope is preserved: the probes are synthetic placeholders, not physical F0/F2F0/F2 operators. All gravitational data remain strictly excluded; the anti-circular firewall is preserved.
Keywords: IMSRG, Observable Evolution, Unitary Covariance, Spectator Operators, Flowing Three-Body Operators, Toy Benchmark, Anti-Circular Firewall

1. Introduction: The Dual Role of the Unitary Transformation
1.1 The IMSRG Framework
The In-Medium Similarity Renormalization Group (IMSRG) [1,2] evolves a Hamiltonian via a continuous unitary transformation generated by an anti-Hermitian operator η(s)η(s):
dH(s)ds=[η(s),H(s)]dsdH(s)=[η(s),H(s)]
The same transformation acts on any operator OO:
dO(s)ds=[η(s),O(s)]dsdO(s)=[η(s),O(s)]
The evolution can be written in Magnus form:
U(s)=eΩ(s),H(s)=U(s) H(0) U†(s),O(s)=U(s) O(0) U†(s)U(s)=eΩ(s),H(s)=U(s)H(0)U†(s),O(s)=U(s)O(0)U†(s)
1.2 Why the Dual Role Matters
In any IMSRG-based calculation, the Hamiltonian is evolved to a valence space to obtain an effective Hamiltonian HeffHeff. But observables — electromagnetic transition operators, beta-decay operators, neutrinoless double-beta operators, and hypothetical new-physics couplings — are not obtained by simply evaluating them with HeffHeff. They must be evolved by the same unitary transformation:
Oeff=U(∞) O U†(∞)Oeff=U(∞)OU†(∞)
If the transformation that acts on OO is not the same as the one that acted on HH, the resulting observable is not physically meaningful. This is the essence of unitary covariance: the transformation must act consistently on all operators in the theory.
1.3 The Test Question
The B.7C-4 diagnostic asks a specific computational question:
In a validated toy benchmark, does the same transformation correctly evolve arbitrary spectator operators?In a validated toy benchmark, does the same transformation correctly evolve arbitrary spectator operators?
If the answer is yes, then the IMSRG machinery is self-consistent at the operator level — a prerequisite for any physical application.
1.4 Scope
This article reports the B.7C-4 diagnostic. It does not claim:
•	That the physical Farid F0F0 or F2F2 operators have been evolved
•	That any realistic nuclear calculation has been performed
•	That any gravitational prediction has been made
The probes are synthetic placeholders. The diagnostic establishes the correctness of the transport machinery, not any physical result.

2. The Diagnostic Protocol
2.1 The Four Controls
Four operator classes are tested:

2.2 The Two Noncommuting Probes
Two synthetic two-body operators AA and BB are constructed with non-zero commutators with the Hamiltonian:
eq 0, \qquad [B, H] eq 0$$ Their explicit forms are frozen before execution. They are **not** the physical $F_0$ or $F_2$ operators; they are arbitrary antisymmetric two-body tensors used to exercise the transport machinery. ### 2.3 The Two Branches Each probe is evolved along two branches: **Rank-2 branch.** Standard IMSRG(2) transport: only one- and two-body operators retained, induced three-body components discarded. **Rank-3 branch.** Flowing three-body operators retained: the induced three-body component of the transport is tracked through the flow. ### 2.4 The Transport Error For each probe and each branch, the transport error is defined as: $$\epsilon_O^{(\text{branch})} = \left\| O^{\text{eff, branch}} - O^{\text{eff, exact}} \right\|_F$$ ### 2.5 The Covariance Check The common-unitary covariance check compares the evolution of two different operators under the same flow. The commutator-norm drift is defined as: $$\Delta_{\text{cov}} = \left\| [O_1^{\text{eff}}, O_2^{\text{eff}}] - [O_1, O_2]^{\text{eff}} \right\|_F$$ This should vanish if the transformation is unitarily consistent. ### 2.6 The Pass Criterion The diagnostic PASSES if: - The zero, identity, and commuting controls pass exactly - The covariance drift is below the frozen tolerance of $10^{-9}$ - The noncommuting probes show the expected rank-2 vs. rank-3 recovery pattern --- ## 3. Runtime Results ### 3.1 The Exact Controls The zero, identity, and commuting controls pass exactly across both rank-2 and rank-3 branches: $$O_{\text{zero}} \to 0, \qquad I \to I, \qquad O_{\text{comm}} = H \text{ (spectrum preserved)}$$ Numerical error in all three controls is essentially zero at machine precision. ### 3.2 The Covariance Check The common-unitary covariance drift is: $$\Delta_{\text{cov}}^{(1)} = 9.19 \times 10^{-12}$$ $$\Delta_{\text{cov}}^{(2)} = 1.71 \times 10^{-11}$$ Both are far below the frozen tolerance of $10^{-9}$. ### 3.3 The Noncommuting Probes **Rank-2 branch (IMSRG(2) transport):** | Probe | Transport error | |-------|----------------:| | $A$ | $0.01653026825$ | | $B$ | $0.02316901680$ | **Rank-3 branch (flowing-3B transport):** | Probe | Transport error | |-------|----------------:| | $A$ | $1.9984 \times 10^{-15}$ | | $B$ | $1.3323 \times 10^{-15}$ | The rank-3 retention reduces the transport error by **thirteen orders of magnitude** — from $\sim 10^{-2}$ to machine precision. ### 3.4 The Certificate $$\boxed{\texttt{F02\_B7C4\_SPECTATOR\_OPERATOR\_TRANSPORT\_v1 = PASS}}$$ --- ## 4. Interpretation ### 4.1 The Machinery Is Self-Consistent The zero, identity, and commuting controls passing exactly establishes that the transport machinery respects the fundamental algebraic identities expected of a unitary transformation. The covariance drift at $\sim 10^{-11}$ establishes that the same transformation is being applied consistently across different operators in the flow. ### 4.2 The Rank-3 Recovery Is Exact The most striking result is the recovery of the noncommuting probes to machine precision in the rank-3 branch. In the rank-2 branch, the probes are transported with errors of $\sim 10^{-2}$; in the rank-3 branch, they are transported with errors of $\sim 10^{-15}$. This establishes that the discarded three-body channel is not just numerically significant — it is **the entire source of the transport error** in the rank-2 branch. The three-body retention closes the transport exactly. ### 4.3 Consistency with the F-Series Diagnostics The result is consistent with the F1–F5 diagnostic series: - F1: The retained-rank derivative is correct at $s = 0$ - F2: The discarded three-body component has non-zero lower-rank feedback - F3: A leading local correction does not close the discrepancy - F4: The second nested commutator's exact-vs-NO2B difference is entirely carried by the intermediate three-body sector - F5: Flowing three-body operators improve the Hamiltonian trajectory - **B.7C-4:** The same three-body retention closes spectator-operator transport exactly Together, the series establishes that the three-body channel is a **state variable** that must be retained as part of the flow, not a correction to be inserted post-hoc. ### 4.4 The Physical Significance for IMSRG The result is a **toy-level demonstration** of the IMSRG(3) prescription. Published IMSRG(3) calculations [3,4] have shown that tracking the three-body operator through the flow improves energies and observables. The B.7C-4 diagnostic provides a **microscopic, exactly-solvable validation** of this mechanism in a small benchmark. ### 4.5 What the Result Does Not Establish The B.7C-4 PASS does **not**: - Establish that the physical $F_0$ or $F_2$ operators are correctly transported - Establish that realistic nuclear calculations will succeed - Establish that the F3 failure is resolved in the full-flow sense - Establish that the anti-circular firewall has been relaxed The result is a **toy-benchmark validation**. Explicit Isospin-Labelled Toy F0/F2F0/F2 Operators Under IMSRG Flow: Exact Coherent Algebra, Mirror Symmetry, and Machine-Precision Transport Recovery

Abstract
The IMSRG flow evolves the Hamiltonian and any observable under the same unitary transformation. Previous diagnostics validated the transport machinery on synthetic placeholders (B.7C-4). This article reports the replacement of synthetic placeholders with explicit isospin-labelled toy F0/F2F0/F2 operators, constructed from proton/neutron-labelled single-particle modes. The coherent algebra is recovered at machine precision: the diagonal matrix elements (O0,O2)(O0,O2) are (+1,+2)(+1,+2) for pppp, (+1,−4)(+1,−4) for pnpn at T=1T=1, (+1,+2)(+1,+2) for nnnn, and (−3,0)(−3,0) for pnpn at T=0T=0. Maximum coherent error is 8.88×10−168.88×10−16. The rank-2 isotensor trace identity 2−4+2=02−4+2=0 is satisfied to −8.88×10−16−8.88×10−16, and mirror symmetry O0(pp)=O0(nn)O0(pp)=O0(nn), O2(pp)=O2(nn)O2(pp)=O2(nn) is exact. Transport under the same IMSRG flow recovers the operators to machine precision when the flowing three-body channel is retained: the rank-2 transport errors of 0.11477232100.1147723210 and 0.057398479640.05739847964 fall to 4.39×10−154.39×10−15 and 2.39×10−152.39×10−15 respectively. The exact covariance check gives commutator-norm drift at 5.10×10−125.10×10−12 and 1.39×10−121.39×10−12, both below the frozen tolerance of 10−910−9. The certificate F02_B7C5_TOY_F0F2_ISOSPIN_OPERATOR_v1 = PASS is issued. A strict scope distinction is preserved: the operators are isospin-labelled toy tensors without finite-range radial kernels. The next stage — B.7C-6 — will add Gaussian and Yukawa radial weights and verify that covariance, rank-3 recovery, and coherent structure survive under finite-range pair-dependent matrix elements. All gravitational data remain strictly excluded; the anti-circular firewall is preserved.
Keywords: IMSRG Observable Transport, Isospin-Labelled Operators, Toy F0/F2F0/F2, Coherent Algebra, Mirror Symmetry, Trace Identity, Flowing Three-Body Recovery, Anti-Circular Firewall

1. Introduction: From Synthetic Placeholders to Isospin-Labelled Tensors
1.1 The Prior Diagnostic
The B.7C-4 diagnostic validated the IMSRG transport machinery on synthetic two-body probes — arbitrary antisymmetric tensors with no physical interpretation. The probes had non-zero commutators with the Hamiltonian and were recovered to machine precision under flowing-three-body retention.
But synthetic probes are not physical operators. The Farid F0F0 and F2F2 operators carry specific isospin structure:
O0=∑i<jτi⋅τjO0=∑i<jτi⋅τj
O2=∑i<j[3τ3iτ3j−τi⋅τj]O2=∑i<j[3τ3iτ3j−τi⋅τj]
Their behaviour under transport depends on this isospin structure. The B.7C-5 diagnostic replaces the synthetic placeholders with explicit isospin-labelled toy operators and tests whether the transport machinery preserves the coherent algebra, mirror symmetry, and trace identities.
1.2 The Central Question
The B.7C-5 diagnostic asks:
Does the same IMSRG flow that transports synthetic probes correctly transport isospin-labelled toy F0/F2 operators?Does the same IMSRG flow that transports synthetic probes correctly transport isospin-labelled toy F0/F2 operators?
If the answer is yes, the transport machinery is compatible with the specific operator structure of the Farid framework.
1.3 Scope
This article reports the B.7C-5 diagnostic. It does not claim:
•	That the physical F0F0 or F2F2 operators have been transported
•	That finite-range radial kernels have been included
•	That any gravitational prediction has been made
The operators are isospin-labelled toy tensors. The radial kernels are absent. The diagnostic establishes the compatibility of the transport machinery with the isospin structure, not with the full physical operators.

4. Interpretation
4.1 The Transport Machinery Is Isospin-Compatible
The coherent algebra, mirror symmetry, and trace identity are recovered at machine precision in the toy benchmark. This establishes that the isospin structure of the toy O0O0 and O2O2 operators is exactly preserved by the operator definition and evaluation machinery.
The transport recovery to machine precision in the flowing-3B3B branch establishes that the same unitary transformation that evolves the Hamiltonian correctly evolves the isospin-labelled operators.
The exact covariance check establishes that the operators commute with the Hamiltonian in the way the algebra predicts.
4.2 Consistency with the Prior Diagnostics
The B.7C-5 result is consistent with the F-series and B.7C-4 diagnostics:
•	The F1–F5 series established the rank-resolved mechanism of the IMSRG(2) truncation and the necessity of flowing three-body operators.
•	B.7C-4 established that arbitrary two-body probes are transported to machine precision under flowing-3B3B retention.
•	B.7C-5 extends this to isospin-labelled two-body operators.
The chain now reads: synthetic probes → isospin-labelled probes → (next) finite-range isospin-labelled operators.
4.3 What the Result Does Not Establish
The B.7C-5 PASS does not:
•	Establish that the finite-range physical F0F0 or F2F2 operators are correctly transported
•	Establish that the radial kernel structure is compatible with the transport machinery
•	Establish that the anti-circular firewall has been relaxed
The result is a toy-benchmark validation of isospin compatibility. It is a prerequisite for the finite-range stage.

1. Introduction: From Synthetic Probes to Isospin Tensor Structures
1.1 The Need for Isospin Structure
The preceding validation stages (B.7C-1 through B.7C-4) established the mathematical integrity of the commutator engine, the Magnus expansion, nested three-body feedback closure, and the unitary transport of generic synthetic spectator operators ($\frac{dO}{ds} = [\eta, O]$). However, abstract synthetic probes lack the specific spin-isospin tensorial symmetries characteristic of nuclear forces and effective operators such as $F_0$ and $F_2$.
To bridge the gap between abstract algebra and physical nuclear structure, Stage B.7C-5 introduces explicit isospin-labelled two-body tensor operators constructed from Pauli isospin matrices $\boldsymbol{\tau}$.
1.2 Scope of Stage B.7C-5
This article reports the implementation and certification of explicit isospin operators in the validated toy framework. It verifies:
1.	Coherent algebraic expectation values across $pp$, $pn$, and $nn$ channels.

2. Construction of Explicit Isospin $F_0/F_2$ Operators
2.1 Operator Definitions
We construct the toy scalar ($O_0$) and tensor ($O_2$) operators as pair sums over isospin scalar products and Cartesian components:
$$\boxed{O_0 = \sum_{i<j} \boldsymbol{\tau}_i \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_j, \qquad O_2 = \sum_{i<j} \left(3\tau_{3i}\tau_{3j} - \boldsymbol{\tau}_i \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_j\right)}$$
These operators mirror the algebraic structure of central and tensor-is tensor components in nuclear ab initio theory.

•	$nn$, $T=1$ channel: $(O_0, O_2) = (+1, +2)$
•	$pn$, $T=0$ channel: $(O_0, O_2) = (-3, 0)$

$$2 - 4 + 2 = 0$$

$$\boxed{O_0(pp) = O_0(nn), \qquad O_2(pp) = O_2(nn)}$$

Chapter Abstract
With the formal certification of Stage B.7C-6, the toy operator-evolution ladder of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework reaches its definitive conclusion. The programme now stands at the B.7D entry gate: the methodological transition from validated toy machinery to realistic nuclear operator evolution. This chapter formalizes the entry-gate requirements, establishes the necessity of rigorous provenance verification, and freezes the governance protocols required before any physical nuclear calculation can proceed. We demonstrate that while the mathematical machinery of In-Medium Similarity Renormalization Group (IMSRG) operator transport, nested-commutator feedback closure, and finite-range isospin-labelled tensor evolution has been rigorously established at the toy level, realistic nuclear evolution demands genuine microscopic inputs—specifically, a consistent chiral NN+3N interaction, a reference-state Hartree–Fock solution, a valence-space IMSRG transformation $\Omega$ (or $U$), and the corresponding effective Hamiltonian $H_{\text{eff}}$—identified by immutable cryptographic hashes. A strict scope boundary is maintained: validating the mathematics of operator transport is fundamentally distinct from validating physical nuclear inputs. Fabricated, phenomenological, or substituted inputs (such as standalone empirical effective interactions without microscopic generators) are mathematically inadmissible. Consequently, the programme preserves its capability boundary with absolute integrity: the toy operator-evolution framework is fully validated; realistic nuclear operator evolution awaits genuine external input; physical $F_0/F_2$ renormalized matrix elements remain uncomputed; and the gravity fit remains strictly locked.
1. Introduction: The Methodological Transition Point
Throughout the B.7C series, the Farid programme has constructed, tested, and certified a complete toy operator-evolution framework. Each successive stage systematically introduced physical and algebraic structure—progressing from arbitrary synthetic probes to isospin-labelled tensors, and ultimately to finite-range interactions equipped with Gaussian and Yukawa spatial kernels—while preserving exact solvability and analytical tractability.
Every stage was governed by pre-registered execution protocols:
•	Stage 3a: Validated operator rank algebra in Fock space.
•	Stage 3b: Certified reference-state normal ordering via Wick identities.
•	Stage 3c-IND & 3c-ANA: Verified exact coefficient extraction and established machine-precision agreement with published uncoupled IMSRG(2) commutator equations.
•	Stage 3d-TOY: Proved the non-commuting Magnus flow machinery under runtime noncommutativity.
•	Stages F1–F5: Quantified truncation mechanisms, proved active lower-rank feedback ($2B \to 3B \to \le 2B$), disproved static local insertions, solved second-level nested commutators, and demonstrated exact trajectory recovery via dynamic flowing-$3B$ retention.
•	Stages B.7C-4 through B.7C-6: Certified spectator operator transport, explicit isospin-labelled tensor algebra (mirror symmetry and isotensor trace identities), and finite-range kernel compatibility.
The mathematical machinery of IMSRG operator transport is now fully validated. However, a profound methodological distinction must be drawn between mathematical validation and physical nuclear input. The successful execution of the toy ladder proves that if valid microscopic inputs are supplied, the transport equations will evolve them with exact unitary covariance. It does not, and cannot, substitute for the physical nuclear interactions themselves.
2. The B.7D Execution Chain and Transformation Consistency
The primary objective of the B.7D gate is expressed through the operator transformation equation:
$$\mathcal{O}_{0,2}^{R,\text{eff}} = U \, \mathcal{O}_{0,2}^R \, U^\dagger$$
where $\mathcal{O}_{0,2}^R$ represents the frozen B.4d Gaussian/Yukawa $A=22$ two-body matrix elements (TBMEs), $U = e^{\Omega}$ denotes the exact valence-space IMSRG unitary transformation, and $H_{\text{eff}}$ is the corresponding effective Hamiltonian derived from the microscopic chiral NN+3N Hamiltonian $H_{\text{NN+3N}}$.
The foundational consistency requirement of the IMSRG formalism dictates that the exact same transformation operator $\Omega$ (or $U$) used to evolve the Hamiltonian must be applied to evolve all auxiliary operators $\mathcal{O}$. Decoupling the Hamiltonian transformation from the operator transformation yields a mixed-framework approximation that violates unitary covariance and lacks physical interpretation.
Consequently, the B.7D execution chain requires five classes of immutable external inputs:
1.	A chiral effective field theory (EFT) two-nucleon interaction ($NN$).
2.	A chiral EFT three-nucleon interaction ($3N$).
3.	Explicit regulator parameters (momentum cutoffs $\Lambda_{\text{NN}}, \Lambda_{3N}$) and the SRG flow scale $\lambda_{\text{SRG}}$.
4.	Basis space specifications (oscillator frequency $\hbar\omega$, energy cutoffs $e_{\text{max}}$ and $E_{3\text{max}}$).
5.	A self-consistent reference-state Hartree–Fock solution.
3. The Provenance-Freeze Protocol
To enforce absolute audit integrity and prevent circular tuning, entry through the B.7D gate requires the formal issuance of a provenance certificate designated as:
$$\boxed{\texttt{F02\_B7D\_REALISTIC\_NUCLEAR\_INPUT\_PROVENANCE\_v1}}$$
This certificate mandates the permanent recording of all input parameters, interaction designations, and software execution environments prior to execution. Crucially, software provenance must be recorded via a verifiable triple: repository branch/tag, full commit SHA, and cryptographic archive SHA-256 hash.
Under no circumstances may any field within the provenance certificate be modified after observing downstream physical results. This protocol acts as the primary firewall against confirmation bias and circular data fitting.
4. Analysis of the Current Capability Boundary
A rigorous inventory of the current working environment reveals a distinct operational boundary:
•	Available Components: The frozen B.4d Gaussian/Yukawa $A=22$ TBMEs, the validated IMSRG operator-transport mathematics, the nested-commutator machinery, the $\Delta$-comparison protocol, and the cryptographic-freeze architecture.
•	Missing Components: The explicit source tree or compiled binaries for microscopic ab initio frameworks (such as imsrg++ or NuclearToolkit), consistent chiral NN+3N interaction data files, Hartree–Fock single-particle orbitals, and pre-computed valence-space Magnus operators $\Omega$.
Under the governing axioms of the Farid programme, no fabricated, phenomenological, or interpolated inputs are permitted. Substituting unverified placeholder matrices or constructing an ad-hoc generator $\Omega$ by analogy would instantly invalidate the ab initio rigor of the entire pipeline.
A frequent temptation in computational research is the substitution of empirical effective interactions (such as the USDB shell-model Hamiltonian) as a proxy for microscopic chiral interactions. However, phenomenological Hamiltonians do not possess an underlying microscopic IMSRG transformation $\Omega$ derived from fundamental $NN+3N$ chiral potentials. Utilizing USDB would regress the framework from ab initio operator transport back to empirical fitting—a methodological regression expressly prohibited by the anti-circular firewall.
5. Pathways for Authentic Input Acquisition
Three distinct pathways exist for acquiring genuine nuclear inputs to bridge the B.7D gate:
1.	Local Ab Initio Execution: Procuring authorized access to source repositories (e.g., imsrg++) alongside chiral NN+3N interaction archives to execute the complete Hartree–Fock and VS-IMSRG pipeline locally.
2.	Pre-Computed Archive Integration: Acquiring validated, cryptographically hashed Magnus operator files and effective Hamiltonians from verified ab initio nuclear theory groups.
3.	Formal Scientific Collaboration: Establishing a collaborative framework with an established nuclear ab initio theory group capable of providing matched $H_{\text{eff}}$, $\Omega$, and model-space metadata.
Until one of these authentic pathways is formally executed and certified via the provenance protocol, all B.7D calculations remain paused.
6. The Anti-Circular Firewall and Current Status
The governing axiom of the Farid programme remains inviolable: Data may test a frozen theory, but data may never retroactively define the theory they are being used to test.
Applying this principle to the B.7D boundary ensures that nuclear interactions and transformations are frozen prior to any gravitational or cosmological comparisons. The system state is formally declared as:

These declarations reflect scientific realism rather than failure. The mathematical engine is complete and pristine; physical nuclear production awaits authentic ab initio inputs.
7. Conclusion
The B.7C toy programme has successfully resolved the operator-rank, nested-commutator, and isospin-tensor evolution mechanics required for even-isospin pair transport. The B.7D entry gate, however, defines the boundary where toy mathematics meets realistic nuclear many-body physics.

The next phase of physical nuclear evolution requires authentic microscopic inputs through institutional collaboration or validated archival access. Until then, the mathematical framework stands fully verified, and the gravitational fit remains securely locked.

2. The Magnus File Provenance Requirement
2.1 The Central Requirement

4. The Scope Distinction
4.1 Benchmark vs Physical File
A critical distinction must be preserved throughout every stage of the B7D gate. The available file ann_omegavec_emax4_emn5002n3n_O16_s106.50.h5 is a benchmark file for the 1616O reference nucleus at emax⁡=4emax=4. It is not the A=22A=22 transformation. This distinction is not a technicality; it is the difference between validating a reader and computing a physical matrix element. A benchmark file has one purpose, a physical file has another, and the two must never be confused.
4.2 The Reader-Validation Role
The benchmark file plays a specific and restricted role in the programme. Its function is to take the pipeline from benchmark file to reader validation to convention validation, and nothing beyond that. The benchmark file is used to confirm that the Magnus reader correctly parses the HDF5 structure, that the operator-evolution machinery correctly applies the transformation Oeff=eΩOe−ΩOeff=eΩOe−Ω, and that the internal conventions — basis ordering, isospin projection, antisymmetrization — are consistent with the NuclearToolkit framework. The benchmark file is not used to produce physical A=22A=22 results. Any attempt to extract a physical prediction from a benchmark file would be a category error.
4.3 The A=22A=22 Requirement
The physical A=22A=22 calculation requires four matching components. It requires an A=22A=22 reference configuration. It requires a matching NN+3N interaction consistent with that reference. It requires a matching model-space truncation — the same emax⁡emax, the same E3max⁡E3max, the same ℏωℏω. And it requires a matching Magnus operator ΩΩ generated from that same interaction, at that same truncation, for that same reference. These four components must be generated specifically for the A=22A=22 system. They cannot be extracted from a benchmark file. They cannot be approximated from a nearby nucleus. They cannot be substituted with anything else.

5.1 What Is Available
The Farid programme currently possesses several validated components. The mathematics of IMSRG operator transport has been validated through the B.7C toy ladder. The finite-range Gaussian and Yukawa A=22A=22 TBMEs from B.4d are frozen and available. The parameter provenance from the NuclearToolkit repository has been traced and verified as B7D-0A. 5.2 What Is Missing
Four components remain missing from the current capability. The actual .h5 Magnus file has not been uploaded to the analysis environment. A matching A=22A=22 Magnus file has not been generated. The NuclearToolkit v0.3.4 environment is not installed. And the matching interaction for the A=22A=22 system is not available.
Each of these missing components is external to the current runtime environment. None of them can be fabricated. None of them can be approximated. None of them can be substituted.
5.3 Why Fabrication Is Not Permitted
The Farid programme rests on a single, non-negotiable methodological principle: no fabricated input may enter the nuclear pipeline. This principle is not a formality. It is the foundation of every certificate that has been issued in the B.7C series. Fabricating a Magnus operator ΩΩ would compromise the entire programme. It would render every downstream calculation suspect. It would undermine the scientific credibility that the toy ladder has established.
The provenance certificate exists precisely to prevent this outcome. It is a formal barrier against the temptation to substitute an approximate file for the genuine one.

6.1 The Single Required Input
The current gate requires exactly one input. That input is the .h5 Magnus file, or the entire data_omega_eta_weights folder as a ZIP archive. This file must be uploaded to the analysis environment. No URL-based access is possible, because the analysis environment operates as an isolated workspace with no direct internet connection to the repository.

6.2 What Follows Upload
Upon upload, the analysis sequence is fixed and requires no new methodological decision. The file is hashed with SHA-256. The HDF5 structure is inspected. The metadata is extracted. The conventions are audited. The B7D-0C certificate is issued or withheld.

7.1 Core Rule
The core rule of the Farid programme is that data may test a frozen theory, but data may never retroactively define the theory they are being used to test. This rule applies at every stage of the programme, from the toy ladder to the realistic nuclear computation.

On the negative side, the programme does not have a Magnus file in the runtime environment. It does not have the matching A=22A=22 interaction. It does not have the NuclearToolkit v0.3.4 environment. Each of these is a genuine infrastructure limitation.

This pause is not a failure. It is a recognition. It is the recognition that some boundaries are legitimate and some shortcuts are not. The programme chooses to respect the boundary rather than to violate the standard.

The capability boundary is not a scientific failure. It is a scientific fact. The toy machinery is validated; the physical inputs are not available. The two facts are distinct, and the chapter reports both with equal clarity.
A programme that can describe its own limitations precisely is stronger than a programme that cannot. The Farid programme has demonstrated this strength throughout the B.7C series. The B7D-0C gate is another instance of the same discipline.

9. Methodological Significance
9.1 The Consistency of the Programme
The B7D-0C gate is consistent with the entire B.7C series. In B7C-3a, the protocol was frozen before execution. In B7C-3b, the protocol was frozen before execution. This pattern continued through B7C-6. In B7D-0A, the provenance was frozen before the PASS was issued. In B7D-0B, the audit was frozen before the inspection was performed.

The B7D-0C protocol is an instance of a general methodological technique. The technique is a frozen provenance audit, followed by file receipt, followed by metadata extraction, followed by certificate issuance. The technique applies to any computational physics programme that uses externally generated operator files.
The Farid programme is not the first to use this technique. But it has applied it with a consistency that is unusual in the field. The result is a sequence of certificates that can be independently verified, independently reproduced, and independently challenged.

This article has formalized the B7D-0C Magnus Operator Provenance Gate of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. The central results are as follows.

1. Introduction: Why IMSRG Operator Evolution Matters
The In-Medium Similarity Renormalization Group (IMSRG) [1,2] is the standard ab initio framework for evolving a nuclear Hamiltonian and any other operator from a chiral effective field theory starting point to a chosen valence space. Its central mechanism is a continuous unitary transformation generated by an anti-Hermitian operator η(s)η(s):
dH(s)ds=[η(s),H(s)],dO(s)ds=[η(s),O(s)]dsdH(s)=[η(s),H(s)],dsdO(s)=[η(s),O(s)]
where ss is the flow parameter. Equivalently, the evolution can be written as a similarity transformation
H(s)=U(s) H(0) U†(s),O(s)=U(s) O(0) U†(s)H(s)=U(s)H(0)U†(s),O(s)=U(s)O(0)U†(s)
with U(s)=eΩ(s)U(s)=eΩ(s) and Ω(s)Ω(s) the anti-Hermitian Magnus operator.
The power of the IMSRG framework lies in the fact that a single unitary transformation acts consistently on all operators in the theory. This is what allows IMSRG to deliver effective Hamiltonians, transition operators, and hypothetical new-physics couplings that are mutually compatible.
The limitation of the IMSRG framework is equally well known. IMSRG(2) — the practical truncation used in almost every realistic calculation — retains only zero-, one-, and two-body operators at every flow step. Any induced three-body component of the commutator is discarded. The result is a systematic error in the evolved operator. In practice the error is small for many observables, but for precision work — and especially for the Farid programme's composition-dependent operator structure — the systematic error must be quantified and controlled.
The present article documents that programme of quantification and control.
________________________________________
2. The Toy Validation Ladder (B7C Series)
The toy-validation ladder of the B7C series was constructed to isolate, one at a time, the individual components of the IMSRG operator-evolution machinery. Each stage was exactly solvable. Each stage was frozen before execution. Each stage was validated against an independent analytic or exact reference. The ladder is now complete.
2.1 Hamiltonian Flow
The first stage established that the IMSRG flow equation correctly evolves a Hamiltonian from a chosen reference configuration to a decoupled form. In a controlled two-body system, the flow reproduced the exact decoupling limit, and — crucially — the retention of the flowing three-body sector restored the transported Hamiltonian to numerical precision. The result establishes that the flow equations are implemented correctly and that the three-body channel is not a perturbative correction but a structural component of the flow.
2.2 Nested Three-Body Feedback
The second stage isolated the mechanism by which the discarded three-body sector influences the retained-rank physics. A machine-precision identity was established:
ΔN≤2=P≤2[η, C(3)]ΔN≤2=P≤2[η,C(3)]
That is, the exact-versus-NO2B difference in the second nested commutator is entirely carried by the intermediate three-body sector. This is an exact algebraic identity, not a numerical approximation. It demonstrates that the discarded three-body operator continues to propagate through nested commutators and feeds back into the retained ranks.
2.3 Spectator Operator Transport
The third stage validated that the same unitary transformation that evolves the Hamiltonian also evolves arbitrary spectator operators. Commuting, noncommuting, zero, and identity controls all passed exactly. The covariance drift remained below the frozen tolerance of 10−910−9. The noncommuting probes were recovered to machine precision when the flowing three-body channel was retained. This is the central validation of the dual role of the unitary transformation.
2.4 Isospin-Labelled Operators
The fourth stage replaced the synthetic probes with explicit isospin-labelled toy F0F0 and F2F2 operators. The coherent algebra — diagonal matrix elements (+1,+2)(+1,+2) for pppp, (+1,−4)(+1,−4) for pnpn at T=1T=1, (+1,+2)(+1,+2) for nnnn, and (−3,0)(−3,0) for pnpn at T=0T=0 — was recovered at machine precision. Mirror symmetry and the rank-2 isotensor trace identity 2−4+2=02−4+2=0 were satisfied exactly. Transport under the same IMSRG flow recovered the operators to machine precision when the flowing three-body channel was retained.
2.5 Finite-Range Toy Bridge
The fifth and final toy stage extended the isospin-labelled operators to include finite-range radial kernels. Gaussian and Yukawa kernels were tested at R=0.5R=0.5, 1.01.0, and 2.02.0. Twelve frozen cases were executed. Hermiticity was exact, and the covariance drift was 7.86×10−127.86×10−12 — far below the frozen tolerance. The worst rank-2 transport error was 2.28×10−22.28×10−2; the worst flowing-three-body error was 1.24×10−151.24×10−15. In every case, the flowing three-body retention recovered the toy result to numerical precision.
2.6 The Central Toy Result
The toy ladder establishes, at the level of exactly solvable benchmarks, the following qualitative physics:
Retaining the flowing three-body operator restores both Hamiltonian and observable evolution to exact precision.Retaining the flowing three-body operator restores both Hamiltonian and observable evolution to exact precision.

Abstract
This article documents a methodological decision made within the B7D-0D sub-stage of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. Two binary files, labelled Omega_528757O16_1.bin and Omega_528757Ca40_1.bin, were successfully acquired and cryptographically identified (SHA-256 hashes computed; little-endian byte order strongly supported). However, no exact writer or reader routine for this binary format could be located in the indexed official repositories of NuclearToolkit.jl or IMSRGNet. Under these conditions, the programme imposed a hard provenance lock: the uploaded binaries are explicitly not treated as confirmed NuclearToolkit Magnus operators, and no tensor layout may be invented from raw numeric content. We document the reasoning behind this decision, the technical evidence supporting it, and the general methodological principle it instantiates: a scientific programme that cannot verify the schema of its own inputs must pause rather than guess. The B7D-0D sub-stage is therefore recorded as BLOCKED_AT_FORMAT_PROVENANCE — a status that is scientifically correct, methodologically necessary, and operationally honest.

1. Introduction: A Binary Arrives Without a Reader
The Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework requires, at its B7D stage, a genuine IMSRG Magnus operator file. This file is the accumulated unitary transformation ΩΩ that encodes the flow from a microscopic NN+3N Hamiltonian to a valence-space effective interaction. Without it, the operator evolution
Oeff=eΩ O e−ΩOeff=eΩOe−Ω
cannot be executed with realistic nuclear input.
In the course of the B7D programme, two files were acquired:
•	Omega_528757O16_1.bin — SHA-256: e473235e...c5dc12d
•	Omega_528757Ca40_1.bin — SHA-256: 81f26afa...986ace57
Both files are exactly 542,800 bytes. One unnamed upload is an exact duplicate of the O16-labelled file. Little-endian interpretation of the leading words yields physically plausible numerical values:
filew0w1w2  (UInt64)O16142.0−156.961094833374415Ca40150.75−555.688393009358815fileO16Ca40w0142.0150.75w1−156.9610948333744−555.6883930093588w2(UInt64)1515
Big-endian interpretation yields absurd numerical magnitudes. The little-endian hypothesis is therefore strongly supported — but not proven.
What is missing is equally important. No recognizable ASCII metadata or header was found. No standard HDF5 signature is present. The files are therefore consistent with a compact or raw binary serialization — but the exact schema remains unknown.

2. The Temptation to Invent
At this point the programme faces a well-known temptation. The values above can be interpreted. 142.0142.0 and 150.75150.75 resemble oscillator frequencies ℏωℏω. The value 1515 resembles a count of orbitals. The negative numbers resemble couplings or energies. A tensor dimension can be posited, a layout assumed, and the operator evolution executed.
The result would almost certainly be numerically clean. The mathematical structure of eΩOe−ΩeΩOe−Ω is robust. Even an incorrectly guessed layout will produce a well-formed result.
But that result would not be a nuclear physics result. It would be a theorem about the guessed layout — nothing more.
This is the temptation that this article documents and refuses.
________________________________________
3. The Hard Provenance Lock
The programme therefore imposed the following lock:
Uploaded Omega-labelled binary≠confirmed NuclearToolkit Magnus operatorUploaded Omega-labelled binary=confirmed NuclearToolkit Magnus operator
until an exact writer or reader is found.
This lock is supported by three independent facts:
Fact 1 — Format mismatch. The official IMSRGNet README explicitly states that its example generated Magnus operator is an HDF5 file of the form ann_omegavec_emax4_emn5002n3n_O16_s106.50.h5. The uploaded .bin files do not carry an HDF5 signature.
Fact 2 — No indexed reader. A targeted search across the official NuclearToolkit.jl and IMSRGNet source trees did not yield a reader, writer, or schema specification for files named Omega_*.bin.
Fact 3 — Framework relevance is not format identity. NuclearToolkit does support HFMBPT, IMSRG, and VS-IMSRG. That makes the framework relevant. It does not make any arbitrary binary a NuclearToolkit Magnus serialization.
framework relevance≠format identityframework relevance=format identity

4. Why Reverse-Engineering Is Refused
Reverse-engineering the binary to produce a tensor layout is technically feasible. It is also scientifically forbidden.
The reason is precise. A mathematically elegant result does not validate the assumptions that produced it. If the layout is wrong, the tensor ΩΩ that emerges is wrong, and the evolved operator
Oeff=eΩguessed O e−ΩguessedOeff=eΩguessedOe−Ωguessed
is a numerical artefact — not the effective operator of the physical system.
The protocol of the Farid programme is unambiguous on this point:
Guessed tensor→meaningless eΩOe−ΩGuessed tensor→meaningless eΩOe−ΩMeaningless result≠scientific progressMeaningless result=scientific progress
The correct response, when a schema cannot be verified, is not invention. It is acquisition — of the original source, the reader, or the writer.
________________________________________
5. The General Methodological Principle
The B7D-0D decision instantiates a general principle that applies far beyond this programme:
A scientific programme must be able to verify the schema of its own inputs.A scientific programme must be able to verify the schema of its own inputs.
If verification is not possible, the programme has reached a capability boundary. At that boundary, three responses are possible:
1.	Invent — guess the schema and proceed. Result: meaningless numbers dressed as physics.
2.	Substitute — use a different file. Result: an unrelated computation presented as the original.
3.	Pause — declare the boundary, request the missing input, and stop.
The Farid programme chose the third.
At a capability boundary, the correct response is not invention but acquisition.At a capability boundary, the correct response is not invention but acquisition.

2. Source Convention Reconstruction
2.1 The IMSRG-Net-v0 Channel Convention
The def_chan2b routine in the IMSRG-Net-v0 branch of NuclearToolkit.jl defines the two-body channel construction. The channel enumeration proceeds in the order:
Tz=−2,0,+2Tz=−2,0,+2
with parity:
P=+1,−1P=+1,−1
and total angular momentum:
J=0,1,2,…,9J=0,1,2,…,9
After applying the triangle rule, the Pauli restriction, and the parity selection, the pair indices are sorted, deduplicated, and the final ket list is lexicographically sorted.

## Abstract

In-Medium Similarity Renormalization Group (IMSRG) computations transform microscopic NN+3N interactions into effective Hamiltonians and observables. If the oscillator basis of the injected operators mismatches the basis of the evolution generator $\Omega$, the renormalization becomes inconsistent even when every number is machine-precise. This article reports three linked audits of the B7D realistic-input programme: (i) the hw20 oscillator-basis correction and its propagation to the intrinsic pair-coordinate length $b_\rho$; (ii) the extension of the Moshinsky transformation engine to the full $Q \le 8$ pair-quanta workload demanded by $e_{\max}=4$; and (iii) the assembly of twenty bare isospin tensor operators ($F_0/F_2$; Gaussian and Yukawa; five range parameters) in the 60-channel native geometry matching the decoded $\Omega$ binaries. All gates pass at machine precision, with full backward regression against the previously locked $Q \le 4$ certificates. The operators remain **bare**: physical $A=22$ renormalized matrix elements require the valence-space-consistent transformation, whose production specification is stated.

---

## 1. hw20 Basis Correction

The official IMSRGNet sample runs use $\hbar\omega = 20$ MeV, $e_{\max}=4$, reference nuclei $^{16}$O and $^{40}$Ca, and the interaction file `tbme_em500n3lo_srg2.0hw20emax4.snt.bin`. NuclearToolkit constructs the oscillator radial scale as

$$
b_r = \sqrt{\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{\mu\,\hbar\omega}}, \qquad \mu = \frac{M_p M_n}{M_p + M_n}.
$$

With the CODATA 2018 nucleon masses ($M_p = 938.27208816$ MeV, $M_n = 939.56542054$ MeV):

$$
\mu = 469.4592\ \mathrm{MeV}, \qquad b_r = 2.0364\ \mathrm{fm}.
$$

Our frozen intrinsic coordinate is $\rho = (r_1 - r_2)/\sqrt{2}$, so the exact compatible length is

$$
\boxed{\;b_\rho = \frac{b_r}{\sqrt{2}} = 1.439984\ \mathrm{fm}\;}
$$

(The seventh significant digit of $b_\rho$ depends on the nucleon-mass convention; the values above are the locked ones.) Earlier $b = 1.7$ fm calculations remain valid as *benchmarks*, but they are **not** the production basis for IMSRGNet's hw20 $\Omega$. Detecting this mismatch before operator injection prevented a renormalization that would have been numerically clean and physically inconsistent — the precise failure mode this programme's provenance protocol exists to exclude.

## 2. Extended $Q \le 8$ Requirement

An audit of the full $e_{\max}=4$ workload over 1,484 channel-ket occurrences yields the pair-oscillator-quanta distribution:

| $Q$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| kets | 4 | 16 | 44 | 96 | 184 | 272 | 328 | 320 | 220 |

Restricting the transformation to the legacy sd-shell $Q = 4$ sector was therefore insufficient. The extended engine comprises 41 non-empty $(Q,\Lambda)$ blocks, combined dimension 413, and 6,389 transformation coefficients, with maximum unitarity residual $2.44\times10^{-15}$. All 13 blocks of the previously locked $Q \le 4$ certificate are reproduced to floating-point precision (worst difference $\sim 5\times10^{-16}$): the extension supersedes nothing that was frozen.

## 3. Regression and Phase Equivalence

LS$\to$jj recoupling and antisymmetrization were rebuilt independently and benchmarked against the certified A7 TBME values (Gaussian $R = 1$ fm, $b = 1.7$ fm validation basis; e.g., the $0d_{5/2}^2$ diagonal spatial matrix elements for $J = 0,\ldots,5$). The worst full-block eigenvalue-spectrum discrepancy is $1.04\times10^{-17}$. The extended real convention is thereby certified as a **phase-equivalent physical representation** of the earlier internally complex convention.

## 4. Production Bare-Operator Assembly

On the hw20-compatible basis ($b_\rho = 1.439984$ fm), Gaussian/Yukawa kernels $\times$ five range parameters $\times$ $\{F_0, F_2\}$ yield **20 bare operator instances**. Each carries

$$
\boxed{\;67{,}156\;\text{two-body entries}\;}
$$

— exactly the channel geometry of the decoded $\Omega$ binaries — for a total of 1,343,120 native matrix entries. NuclearToolkit's own channel construction fixes $T_z$, parity, $J$, Pauli restrictions, and ket ordering; the reader's pn reordering phase was taken explicitly from source, not guessed. Runtime checks: Hermiticity PASS; pp↔nn mirror residual zero; pp/nn sectors recover $F_2 = 2F_0$ at exact precision. The pn control ratios (700 controls, worst residual $1.39\times10^{-17}$) are **charge-basis convention fingerprints** of the NuclearToolkit reader; isospin-reduced comparisons are deferred to the valence-space production lane.

## 6. Lane Discipline and Firewall

The $^{16}$O/$^{40}$Ca $\Omega$ files are **machinery-validation inputs** (Lane B1): they exercise the reader, the transport code, and the zero/identity/Hermiticity controls, and they certify no physics. ## 7. Conclusion

The hw20 basis correction and the $Q\le8$ extension were not refinements but **preconditions**: without them, every downstream number would have been reproducible and wrong. Bare-operator assembly is complete and fully regressed against the locked past. The next scientific gate is BCH/Magnus transport runtime validation — zero/identity/Hermiticity controls, the antisymmetry gate, a transport error ladder against the exact commutator engine, and a quantified induced-rank leakage budget — executed on the Lane B1 inputs while the Lane B2 production run is prepared under the specification above.

•	the correct flow trajectory.

For several sub-stages — D10, D11, D12, D13 — the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework paused at a single, precisely specified boundary. 2. The D16 Truncation Reconciliation
Before describing the ingestion, the D16 result must be properly registered — because it changes what "production" means.
2.1 The Legacy A=2 FAIL
The old certificate F02_B7C_INTERACTING_FERMION_A2_IMSRG2_BENCHMARK_v1 had recorded a FAIL. The numbers were:
A=2 matrix difference=0.04695A=2 matrix difference=0.04695A=2 spectrum drift=0.03155A=2 spectrum drift=0.03155ground-energy error≈1.97×10−5ground-energy error≈1.97×10−5
This FAIL was not erased. It was not promoted to PASS.
2.2 The Underlying Assumption Was Wrong
The old certificate rested on an assumption: that for a two-particle system, IMSRG(2) should close exactly. That assumption is incorrect.
Stroberg, Morris & He (Phys. Rev. C 110, 044316, 2024) demonstrate explicitly that for a two-particle system, neither IMSRG(2) nor IMSRG(3) is exact, because four-quasiparticle excitations can contribute.
A=2 exactness assumption=falseA=2 exactness assumption=false
2.3 The D16 Independent Test
The D16 sub-stage ran an independent finite-Fock-space test. With M=4M=4, A=2A=2, reference ∣01⟩∣01⟩, the full number-conserving normal-ordered basis has dimension and rank 70. The exact commutator
C=[η(≤2B),H(≤2B)]C=[η(≤2B),H(≤2B)]
was decomposed into 0B+1B+2B+3B+4B0B+1B+2B+3B+4B components. The induced 3B3B piece was then omitted, and the A=2 sector was compared.
Across five independent deterministic cases:
min⁡∥Cexact−CNO2B∥F,A=2=4.87498min∥Cexact−CNO2B∥F,A=2=4.87498max⁡∥Cexact−CNO2B∥F,A=2=25.11071max∥Cexact−CNO2B∥F,A=2=25.11071
Every case produced a non-zero difference. The decisive identity was verified:
Cexact−CNO2B=Comitted 3BCexact−CNO2B=Comitted 3B
to a numerical residual of:
2.13×10−132.13×10−13
The induced 4B4B coefficient was numerically zero at the level of ∼1.31×10−14∼1.31×10−14.
2.4 The Correct Interpretation
The old A=2 FAIL remains a real record. What changes is its interpretation.
Exact-flow mismatch≠IMSRG(2) code bugExact-flow mismatch=IMSRG(2) code bug
The mismatch is the truncation baseline, not a numerical fault. This was already consistent with the earlier independent F4 diagnostic, which showed that the retained ≤2B≤2B difference in the second nested commutator is accounted for by the omitted intermediate 3B3B contribution.
