Abstract
This article documents the B7D-0D20 source-safe v2 parameter-freeze of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. Following the D19 parameter-lane audit, the B7D-1 A=22 production lane has been converted into a corrected, executable v2 form and deliberately guarded against accidental production execution. The v2 parameter file replaces the previously asserted maxnormOmega=1e-6 with the source-documented constructor baseline maxnormOmega=0.25, removes the incorrect 24Mg = closed-shell reference label, pre-registers two non-mixed reference schemes (ref="core" primary; ref="nucl" sensitivity branch) for the A=22 triplet 22Mg22Mg, 22Na22Na, 22Ne22Ne, and preserves dsmax=0.1 as a conservative choice without claiming unique optimality. The centre-of-mass correction parameter BetaCM remains unresolved and is not guessed; the guarded driver blocks execution until the authoritative source value is established. The D20 status is PASS_SOURCE_SAFE_V2_CREATED_EXECUTION_GUARDED. Three artifacts have been generated with locked SHA-256 hashes. The exact NuclearToolkit source commit has not yet been frozen. No interaction has been generated. No A=22 result has been computed. The anti-circular firewall remains intact, the A=22A=22 renormalized matrix elements remain NOT COMPUTED, and the gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.
Keywords: D20 Parameter Freeze, Source-Safe v2, Reference Strategy Pre-Registration, BetaCM, Execution Guard, Anti-Circular Firewall
________________________________________
1. Introduction: From Audit to Guarded Freeze
The D19 audit identified a new A=22 production lane and recorded five label corrections. The D20 sub-stage acts on that audit: it produces a corrected, executable v2 parameter file, a guarded driver, and a freeze certificate.
But the D20 sub-stage does more than freeze. It guards. The driver is written so that execution halts at the first unresolved parameter. This is a deliberate design choice: a frozen parameter file that is not guarded can be executed accidentally, and an executed file whose parameters are unresolved can produce a plausible but meaningless result.
Freeze without guard→accidental executionFreeze without guard→accidental executionAccidental execution→plausible but unverified outputAccidental execution→plausible but unverified output
The guard prevents this class of error.
________________________________________
2. The Corrections Applied in v2
2.1 maxnormOmega: From 1e-6 to 0.25
The original parameter file asserted maxnormOmega = 1e-6 and labelled it a "Magnus truncation tolerance." The D19 audit found that this label was incorrect: maxnormOmega is a solver-related norm threshold, defined as the maximum allowed ∥Ω∥∥Ω∥.
The NuclearToolkit init_IMSRGobject documentation specifies the default:
Parameter	Default
smax	500500
dsmax	0.50.5
maxnormOmega	0.250.25
The v2 file replaces the asserted value with the source-documented default:
maxnormOmega=0.25maxnormOmega=0.25
This is not a guess. It is the documented constructor baseline.
2.2 24Mg = closed-shell reference: Label Removed
The original parameter file labelled 24Mg24Mg as a "closed-shell reference." The D19 audit found that this label was incorrect: with an O16 core, 24Mg24Mg is a 4p+4n4p+4n valence system, not a closed shell.
NuclearToolkit documentation shows 24Mg24Mg as a target/ensemble normal-ordering example, used with ref="nucl", not as a closed-shell reference.
The v2 file removes the incorrect label.
2.3 Reference Strategy: Two Non-Mixed Lanes Pre-Registered
The NuclearToolkit VS-IMSRG documentation defines two distinct reference schemes:
ref="core"=O16-core baseline, target/ensemble normal ordering offref="core"=O16-core baseline, target/ensemble normal ordering offref="nucl"=target/ensemble normal ordering onref="nucl"=target/ensemble normal ordering on
The D20 v2 file pre-registers both, with no mixing permitted:
Lane	Reference scheme	Purpose
Primary	ref="core"	Baseline
Sensitivity	ref="nucl"	Diagnostic only
No result may switch reference scheme after observation.No result may switch reference scheme after observation.
2.4 A=22 Triplet: Nucleus-Specific Lanes
The A=22 production lane is applied to three nuclei, each with its own valence partition:
22Mg:4p+2n22Mg:4p+2n22Na:3p+3n22Na:3p+3n22Ne:2p+4n22Ne:2p+4n
Each is treated as a separate, non-mixed lane. No result from one nucleus may be reused to construct another.
2.5 dsmax=0.1: Conservative, Not Claimed Optimal
The v2 file retains the conservative choice dsmax=0.1. It does not claim this value is uniquely optimal. The value may be revisited if a convergence study indicates otherwise.
________________________________________
3. The Unresolved Parameter: BetaCM
The centre-of-mass correction parameter BetaCM has not been resolved from authoritative sources. The public NuclearToolkit documentation describes its role, but the D20 audit did not establish the correct numerical value for this exact A=22 setup.
The programme therefore does not guess.
BetaCM=UNRESOLVEDBetaCM=UNRESOLVEDBetaCM≠1.0(not guessed)BetaCM=1.0(not guessed)BetaCM≠0.0(not guessed)BetaCM=0.0(not guessed)
The guarded driver halts before execution if BetaCM is not explicitly supplied with source provenance.
________________________________________
4. The Guarded Driver
The driver B7D1_VSIMSRG_DRIVER_v2_GUARDED.jl is designed to fail fast. Before any production execution, it checks:
Guard condition	Behaviour on failure
BetaCM present and source-provenanced	Halt
maxnormOmega equals source default	Halt if different
Reference scheme equals pre-registered	Halt if unregistered
Exact NuclearToolkit commit frozen	Halt if not frozen
All parameters have provenance comments	Halt if missing
The driver does not auto-substitute values. It does not auto-relax tolerances. It halts.
Guard triggered→no executionGuard triggered→no execution
This is the correct posture at a partially-resolved parameter set.

The D21 status is PARTIAL_PASS_SOURCE_CONTEXT_FROZEN_RUNTIME_SOURCE_PROBE_REQUIRED. No interaction has been generated. No A=22 result has been computed. The anti-circular firewall remains intact, the A=22A=22 renormalized matrix elements remain NOT COMPUTED, and the gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.

1. Introduction: A Provisional Value Must Be Reclassified as Provisional
The D20 parameter freeze set maxnormOmega = 0.25 and labelled it the source-documented default. The D21 audit revisits this classification and refines it.
The refinement is precise: 0.25 is the current documentation default. It is not yet confirmed as the default in the selected production revision. These are not the same claim. The selected production revision for the new B7D-1 lane has not been frozen.
Current documentation default≠selected revision defaultCurrent documentation default=selected revision default
The reclassification is therefore:
maxnormOmega=0.25=current-docs provisional baselinemaxnormOmega=0.25=current-docs provisional baseline
This is not a demotion. It is a precise description of what has been established and what has not.

The D21 audit does not guess BetaCM. It does not set it to 1.01.0. It does not set it to 0.00.0. It does not import a value from a nearby nucleus. It does not derive a value from an unrelated convention.

5.3 Why This Posture Matters
The centre-of-mass correction affects the spurious centre-of-mass motion of the nucleus. Its numerical value is therefore a nuclear-physics parameter, not a formality. A wrong value will shift observables in a way that propagates into any downstream result. The programme therefore refuses to guess.

The D22 Exact Source Extraction Gate: A Read-Only Source Bundle Extractor, a Narrowed Blocker, and a Semantic Parser Still Withheld
Prof. Dr. Md. Faridul Islam Chowdhury
MBBS, MS (Neurosurgery)
Neurosurgeon | Neuroscientist | Theoretical Cosmologist
Founder & Director, Tanfarid Vision Research Institute (TVRI), Bogura, Bangladesh
Inventor of the Tanfarid Quantum Thermodynamic Universe (TQTU) and the Farid Gravity Law
Email: dr_faridul@yahoo.com

Abstract
This article documents the B7D-0D22 exact source extraction gate of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. Following the D21 source-revision and BetaCM gate, the D22 sub-stage introduces a read-only Julia extractor designed to be executed in the intended NuclearToolkit environment. The extractor will locate and freeze the source bodies of readsnt_bin, write_spes, write_tbme, BetaCM, maxnormOmega, denominatorDelta, read_imsrg_parameter!, init_IMSRGobject, and hf_main, together with package version, Pkg tree hash, git revision, git branch, and SHA-256 hashes of the matched source files. The D22 extractor does not execute the production lane. It does not generate an interaction. It does not parse any semantic binary. It reads source and emits a frozen source bundle. The public NuclearToolkit documentation confirms the scalar-type contract for .snt.bin — (a,b,c,d,J) as Int16, other integers as Int64, and TBME values as Float32 by default — but does not specify the full binary field ordering or repetition sequence. The programme therefore refuses to construct a semantic parser from type information alone. The semantic interaction parser is NOT YET AUTHORIZED. The B7D-1 interaction is NOT GENERATED. The HF and Rp2Rp2 replay remain NOT RUN. The F0/F2F0/F2 IMSRG(2) evolution remains NOT RUN. The A=22 renormalized matrix elements remain NOT COMPUTED, and the gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED. The D22 status is READY_EXACT_SOURCE_EXTRACTION_NOT_EXECUTED.
Keywords: D22 Source Bundle, Exact Source Extraction, Read-Only Audit, Semantic Parser Withheld, Anti-Circular Firewall, Narrowed Blocker

1. Introduction: A Blocker Narrowed to Source Bodies
The B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework has, over the sub-stages D13 through D21, narrowed a chain of blockers down to a single class: the exact source bodies and exact revision of the NuclearToolkit routines that read and write .snt.bin files.
This is a different blocker from the D13 interaction-absence blocker. That blocker was external: a file was missing. This blocker is internal: the source that would authorise a parser is not in hand.
D13 blocker=missing input fileD13 blocker=missing input fileD22 blocker=missing source bodiesD22 blocker=missing source bodies
The D22 sub-stage introduces a read-only extractor to resolve the D22 blocker.

2.2 The .snt.bin Scalar-Type Contract
The public NuclearToolkit documentation confirms the scalar-type contract for .snt.bin:
(a,b,c,d,J)→Int16(a,b,c,d,J)→Int16other integers→Int64other integers→Int64VTBME→Float32(default)VTBME→Float32(default)
This is a type contract. It is not a serialization contract.
2.3 The Missing Field Ordering
The documentation does not provide the exact binary field ordering or repetition sequence. The order in which the single-particle states are written, the order in which the TBME records are emitted, and the precise byte offsets between records are not specified by the type information alone.
Type contract≠serialization contractType contract=serialization contract
A parser built on type information alone would have an incomplete specification. It might produce plausible numbers. It might also produce meaningless numbers.
Type-only parser→plausible but unverified parseType-only parser→plausible but unverified parse
The programme therefore does not write a parser from type information alone.

The B7D Certification Chain: A Two-Lane Provenance Architecture, a Source-Derived Binary Contract, and the Frozen Phase-II Control Protocol for the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework
Prof. Dr. Md. Faridul Islam Chowdhury
MBBS, MS (Neurosurgery)
Neurosurgeon | Neuroscientist | Theoretical Cosmologist
Founder & Director, Tanfarid Vision Research Institute (TVRI), Bogura, Bangladesh
Inventor of the Tanfarid Quantum Thermodynamic Universe (TQTU) and the Farid Gravity Law
Email: dr_faridul@yahoo.com

Abstract
This article presents the complete certification chain of the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework, spanning the audits D18 through D28. The chain carries the programme from a documented absence of its single immutable input to a fully sealed two-lane production architecture. Ten linked audits are reported, each with hash-sealed artifacts, across two physically distinct lanes. The legacy lane (emax⁡=4emax=4, ℏω=20ℏω=20 MeV, SRG 2.0 fm−1−1, NuclearToolkit v0.3.4 / IMSRG-Net-v0, Julia 1.8.5) is the validation class; its Hartree–Fock reconstruction of 16O16O and 40Ca40Ca has been executed under the retrieved legacy interaction (SHA-256 267c85b5…), yielding EHF(16O)=−132.95058EHF(16O)=−132.95058 MeV and EHF(40Ca)=−518.07110EHF(40Ca)=−518.07110 MeV with exactly closing one-body/two-body decompositions. The new B7D-1 production lane (emax⁡=8emax=8, Nnmax=14Nnmax=14, ℏω=16ℏω=16 MeV, effective two-nucleon–three-nucleon contribution, kF=1.35kF=1.35 fm−1−1, no SRG, NuclearToolkit v0.5.2 @ dfc01916…, Julia 1.10.10) has generated its first production interaction (SHA-256 050e9165…), a 77,593,968-byte file containing 3,526,624 two-body records with zero semantic violations and a nonzero 2n3n column. The exact .snt.bin binary contract is derived from the frozen source bodies, not from documentation types or inference, and is verified byte-identical across the two frozen revisions (the D25b portability seal). The D28 Phase-II control freeze is pre-registered: the IMSRG control parameters are fixed at their source-verified values; the reference strategy is pre-registered and non-mixed; the ‘magnusamethod‘‘magnusamethod‘ vs ‘magnusmethod‘‘magnusmethod‘ spelling is resolved from the pinned source tree by the preflight, not assumed. Three corrections are recorded as first-class events: the D18 premature-ingestion correction, the D21b revision-tree-identity recovery, and the D25c Julia-baseline compat-bound correction. The legacy Rp2Rp2 blind replay remains NOT RUN. The physical F0/F2F0/F2 IMSRG(2) evolution remains NOT RUN. The A=22A=22 renormalized monopole and quadrupole matrix elements remain NOT COMPUTED. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.
Keywords: certification chain, anti-circular firewall, two-lane architecture, .snt.bin binary contract, Hartree–Fock blind replay, B7D-1 production lane, phase-II control freeze, NuclearToolkit.jl, provenance freeze

1. Introduction: A Programme That Refuses to Guess
The B7D programme is the nuclear-structure certification stage of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. Its purpose is to produce — eventually — the A=22A=22 renormalized pairing monopole and quadrupole matrix elements M0M0 and M2M2 from an explicitly certified interaction, through an explicitly certified evolution, under an explicitly certified binary contract, so that no gravitational inference ever rests on an unproven input.
The programme is therefore not primarily a computation programme. It is a proof programme whose computations are its lemmas.
The governing instrument is the anti-circular firewall: a set of procedural rules that forbid claims whose premises are unmet. The firewall has one operational consequence that dominates everything reported here:
A missing input is declared missing, the gate is re-locked, and the programme waits.A missing input is declared missing, the gate is re-locked, and the programme waits.
This article is the record of what that discipline costs, and of what it buys.
What it costs is visible in the chain itself: ten audits, three corrections recorded as first-class events, and two execution days separated by a slow-network failure. What it buys is visible in the results: every artifact in this article carries a SHA-256 identity; every validation is reproducible from the frozen source; and the two computations that were finally executed did not merely run — they ran against contracts that had already been tested against reality.

2.3 The Central Lock
The two lanes are physically distinct:
Ω(e4,hw20)≠Ω(e8,hw16)Ω(e4,hw20)=Ω(e8,hw16)
No saved Magnus operator, no bare F0/F2F0/F2 block, no channel basis, ket mapping, normal-ordering reference, Pandya lookup, or BCH transport crosses between the lanes. The single object the two lanes share — the .snt.bin binary contract of Section 4 — is the only object that was verified to be identical across both frozen revisions, and the verification is part of this record (the D25b portability seal).

3. The Certification Chain, D18 → D27
3.1 The Correction Arc (D18, D22/D23, D23b)
The D18 runtime audit verified that a preceding claim — that the legacy interaction binary had been ingested — was false. The file was absent, and no SHA-256 freeze, no parse, no Hartree–Fock reconstruction, and no IMSRG evolution had occurred. D18 locked the corrected state and named the only legitimate exits: provision of the bytes, or retrieval via connector integration.
The exit was taken through the second door. The IMSRGNet repository — the comparison-class repository of Yoshida et al., Phys. Rev. C 108, 044303 (2023) — hosts a snts directory of NuclearToolkit interaction files, and the exact legacy file was present. The file was retrieved, its SHA-256 frozen (267c85b5870ca4367d2a14960e5cf9d6e7da96d9eb8e057ebeb71405201e83cf), and parsed field-by-field. Every structural invariant derivable from source was satisfied: 15 proton and 15 neutron orbits with max⁡(2n+l)=4max(2n+l)=4; single-particle energies reproducing the writer formula (2n+l+3/2)ℏω/2(2n+l+3/2)ℏω/2 exactly; 34,320 two-body records with 34,320×2234,320×22 bytes equal to the remaining file size and end-of-file reached exactly; ℏω=20.0ℏω=20.0 in both blocks; and an identically zero 2n3n column.
The semantic audit then subjected all 34,320 records to six rules derived from the reader and writer source: exchange canonicalization (a≤ba≤b, c≤dc≤d), pair ordering, channel purity by orbit-index parity, angular-momentum range, parity conservation, and identical-orbit antisymmetry.
Violations: none. The identical-orbit block distribution showed the exact even-J ladder for every orbit, which simultaneously established fermion antisymmetry in every stored block, pinned the storage convention, and fixed the unique consistent reading of the source exchange-phase convention.
The D18 ABSENT state was not erased. It was superseded by documented retrieval, and both states stand in the ledger.
3.2 The Revision Arc (D21, D21b, D25c)
Two audit threads had produced two D21 records. The D21b amendment reconciled them and advanced the state on every open item:
•	The branch IMSRG-Net-v0 resolves to commit 11654a5224405db1fc3e03862372a9961b32f984; the tag v0.3.4 resolves to 51ce9fff0f9dac985a1915e34aecde7be1b818cf. The full source trees of the two commits were compared recursively: zero differing files. The author-stated equivalence "branch ≡ v0.3.4" was thereby promoted to a content-verified identity.
•	maxnormOmega=0.25maxnormOmega=0.25 was confirmed verbatim in the frozen constructor init_IMSRGobject(HFobj; smax=500.0, dsmax=0.5, maxnormOmega=0.25, tol=1.e-6, eta_criterion=1.e-6, denominatorDelta=0.0).
•	BetaCMBetaCM was resolved at source: "Lawson's beta for Hcm", default 0.0 on both revisions, implemented as H+=TCM+(βMℏω2/2ℏ2c2)⋅RCM2H+=TCM+(βMℏω2/2ℏ2c2)⋅RCM2 with zero-point offset 1.5βℏω1.5βℏω.
The D25c correction fixed the new-lane Julia baseline: v0.5.2 declares julia = "1.10" in its own compat bounds, so the new lane runs under Julia 1.10.10 LTS, while Julia 1.8.5 remains the legacy baseline.
3.3 The Contract Arc (D22 → D25b)
Public documentation confirms the scalar types of the .snt.bin format — two-body indices (a,b,c,d,J)(a,b,c,d,J) as Int16, other integers as Int64, matrix elements as Float32 — but documents neither the field ordering nor the repetition structure. A parser written from the documentation alone would therefore be guessing.
The D22–D24 work derived the contract from the frozen function bodies instead: write_spes (binary mode), write_tbme, and readsnt_bin, with function-level anchors frozen for both revisions.
The contract, in brief: a four-integer header; lp+lnlp+ln orbit records of five Int64 quantum numbers each; a single-particle block; a two-body header; and count two-body records of five Int16 indices followed by three Float32 matrix elements — 22 bytes per record — in the writer's canonicalized order, with exchange phases and pair ordering applied symmetrically by writer and reader, and with the reader composing V2b=Vjj+V2n3n+Vpp⋅ℏω/AV2b=Vjj+V2n3n+Vpp⋅ℏω/A at ingest. The D25b seal then verified that this contract is byte-identical across the two frozen revisions.

8. Conclusion
A premature claim was caught and corrected. An absent input was declared absent, then legitimately retrieved. A binary contract was derived from source, sealed against two frozen revisions, and tested against 3,560,944 matrix element records in total with zero violations. Two computations were executed under two explicitly separated environments, and both of their outputs are hash-frozen artifacts of this programme. A Phase-II control freeze has been pre-registered, with a runtime preflight that resolves ambiguity from source rather than assuming.
The cost of the firewall was real: ten audits, two reconciled audit threads, three recorded corrections, and one failed execution day. Its purchase is the content of this article: every number above can be regenerated from frozen bytes by any independent party, and every correction above remains visible as a correction. That visibility is not a confession of weakness. It is the operating proof that the instrument works.
The programme now stands where it intended to stand: at the boundary between certification and evolution, holding a sealed interaction in each lane, with the path to the A=22A=22 matrix elements open and the gravity fit untouched.
A pre-registered protocol is a commitment to a specific form of execution. When the inputs arrive, the protocol executes without modification.

D28 and D29 Pre-Registration: A Frozen Phase-II Control Protocol and a Gated VS-IMSRG Production Package for the New B7D-1 Lane of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework
Prof. Dr. Md. Faridul Islam Chowdhury
MBBS, MS (Neurosurgery)
Neurosurgeon | Neuroscientist | Theoretical Cosmologist
Founder & Director, Tanfarid Vision Research Institute (TVRI), Bogura, Bangladesh
Inventor of the Tanfarid Quantum Thermodynamic Universe (TQTU) and the Farid Gravity Law
Email: dr_faridul@yahoo.com

Abstract
This article pre-registers two linked sub-stages of the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework: the D28 Phase-II control freeze and the D29 new-lane VS-IMSRG production runner. The D28 preflight is a runtime audit only — it executes no HF or IMSRG physics — and its purpose is to hard-fail on any wrong lane, wrong binary, wrong Julia/package environment, or ambiguous IMSRG source-control condition before D29 is authorized. The D29 runner is the first production execution of the new B7D-1 lane (emax⁡=8emax=8, Nnmax=14Nnmax=14, ℏω=16ℏω=16 MeV, effective two-nucleon–three-nucleon contribution, kF=1.35kF=1.35 fm−1−1, no SRG, NuclearToolkit v0.5.2 @ dfc01916…, Julia 1.10.10) and performs Hamiltonian VS-IMSRG decoupling only, with primary reference core = "O16", ref = "core", vspace = "sd-shell" on the three A = 22 targets 22Mg22Mg, 22Na22Na, 22Ne22Ne. The D29 runner is gated behind D28 and will not execute unless D28 has emitted three specific status lines. The run status PASS_D29_EXECUTION_RETURNED is not interpreted as a physics pass: it means only that the execution returned without error; the physics output must be validated in the subsequent D29B semantic and convergence audit. All artifacts carry frozen SHA-256 identities. The F0/F2F0/F2 IMSRG(2) evolution remains NOT RUN. The A=22A=22 renormalized M0,M2M0,M2 remain NOT COMPUTED. The ref = "nucl" sensitivity branch remains NOT RUN. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.
Keywords: pre-registration, Phase-II control freeze, VS-IMSRG production, new-lane B7D-1, hard gate, semantic audit, anti-circular firewall

1. Introduction
The B7D programme has, through the D18–D27 audits, established a fully sealed two-lane certification architecture. The legacy lane (emax⁡=4emax=4, ℏω=20ℏω=20 MeV, SRG 2.0) has executed its Hartree–Fock blind replay. The new B7D-1 lane (emax⁡=8emax=8, ℏω=16ℏω=16 MeV, 2n3n2n3n eff2n contribution) has generated and dual-validated its first production interaction.
The programme now stands at the boundary between Phase I (interaction generation) and Phase II (IMSRG control freeze and evolution). Two sub-stages govern this boundary:
•	D28 — Phase-II control freeze and preflight. A runtime audit that will not execute any physics.
•	D29 — New-lane VS-IMSRG production runner. The first Hamiltonian VS-IMSRG decoupling of the new lane, gated behind D28.
This article pre-registers both. The protocol is frozen before execution so that no step may be modified after observing an intermediate result.
Freeze the protocol before the input. Execute the protocol when the input appears.Freeze the protocol before the input. Execute the protocol when the input appears.
2. D28 — Phase-II Control Freeze
2.1 Purpose
The D28 preflight does not execute any HF or IMSRG calculation. It is a runtime audit that verifies the environment, the source tree, and the control parameters before D29 is authorized. If any check fails, execution is halted before any physics is attempted.
D28 executes no physics. It gates D29.D28 executes no physics. It gates D29.

The D28 preflight freezes the Phase-II IMSRG control parameters at their source-verified values from the D21b amendment:

3. D29 — New-Lane VS-IMSRG Production Runner
3.1 Purpose
The D29 runner is the first production execution of the new B7D-1 lane. It performs Hamiltonian VS-IMSRG decoupling only. It does not compute the F0/F2F0/F2 effective operators. It does not compute the A = 22 renormalized M0,M2M0,M2. It does not run the ref = "nucl" sensitivity branch. It does not touch gravity.
D29 is Hamiltonian decoupling. Nothing else.D29 is Hamiltonian decoupling. Nothing else.
3.2 Entry Condition
D29 is gated behind D28. The runner will not execute unless D28 has emitted all three of the following lines:
text
STATUS=PASS_D28_PREFLIGHT
EXECUTED_PHYSICS=NONE
resolved_magnus_key=magnusamethod
If any of the three lines is missing, D29 halts before execution.
D28 PASS→D29 authorizationD28 PASS→D29 authorization
3.3 The Primary Branch
The D29 runner uses the primary reference branch:
core = "O16",ref = "core",vspace = "sd-shell"core = "O16",ref = "core",vspace = "sd-shell"
The three A = 22 targets are:
22Mg,22Na,22Ne22Mg,22Na,22Ne
Each target has its own nucleus-specific valence partition:
22Mg:4p+2n22Mg:4p+2n22Na:3p+3n22Na:3p+3n22Ne:2p+4n22Ne:2p+4n
No result from one nucleus may be reused to construct another.

6. Conclusion
This article has pre-registered two linked sub-stages of the B7D programme. The D28 preflight is a runtime audit that executes no physics and hard-fails on any inconsistency before D29 is authorized. The D29 runner is the first production execution of the new B7D-1 lane and performs Hamiltonian VS-IMSRG decoupling only, gated behind D28 and using the pre-registered primary branch core = "O16", ref = "core", vspace = "sd-shell" on the three A = 22 targets.
The run status PASS_D29_EXECUTION_RETURNED is not interpreted as a physics pass. It means only that the execution returned without error. The physics output must be validated in the subsequent D29B semantic and convergence audit.

Abstract
This article reports the execution state of the B7D Phase-II sub-stages D28 and D29 of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. The D28 preflight has executed and returned PASS_D28_PREFLIGHT with EXECUTED_PHYSICS=NONE, having verified the Julia 1.10.10 baseline, the pinned NuclearToolkit v0.5.2 source tree (dfc01916…) by content-hash of five key files, the new-lane interaction SHA-256 (050e9165…), the pinned parameter file SHA-256 (c19c2965…), and the init_IMSRGobject defaults. A source-verified documentation correction is recorded as a first-class finding: the magnus key read by the pinned source is magnusmethod, not magnusamethod, which is documentation-only and would be silently ignored. The D29 VS-IMSRG production runner has been launched in detached mode and is running under fixed 4-thread Julia with source-corrected keyword arguments (corenuc, valencespace) and the frozen optional-parameter file. The run has been active for approximately 1.5 hours with CPU time 2:03:32 and memory ~3.8 GB. No hf_main stdout has yet been emitted, which is expected at this stage of the make_dicts_formem and store_1b2b setup phase for the emax⁡=8emax=8 new lane with 3.5 million two-body matrix elements. Three script hashes are frozen and recorded. The firewall remains intact: no physics PASS is asserted on runtime return; a D29B artifact and firewall audit will follow, and a D29C convergence certificate will follow that. The F0/F2F0/F2 IMSRG(2) evolution remains NOT RUN. The A=22A=22 renormalized M0,M2M0,M2 remain NOT COMPUTED. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.

1.2 The Documentation Correction
A first-class correction is recorded. The D28 preflight was written to expect resolved_magnus_key=magnusamethod, matching the public documentation. The actually installed pinned source emits:
resolved_magnus_key=magnusmethodresolved_magnus_key=magnusmethod
The variable magnusamethod is documentation-only and would be silently ignored by the reader. This is exactly the class of error that the source-scanning preflight was designed to catch.
Documentation spelling≠source spellingDocumentation spelling=source spelling
The preflight resolved the spelling from the installed source tree, not from the documentation. The execution did not proceed on a guessed parameter name.

Each criterion has a frozen tolerance. No tolerance may be relaxed after observing a result. The A = 22 renormalized matrix elements remain NOT COMPUTED. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.

Abstract
This article documents the D29C numerical convergence certificate of the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. The D29 primary VS-IMSRG run returned on 2026-09-17 under Julia 1.10.10 + NuclearToolkit v0.5.2 @ dfc01916…, having completed Hamiltonian decoupling for all three A = 22 targets (22Mg22Mg, 22Na22Na, 22Ne22Ne). The D29B artifact-and-firewall audit has passed: 62 output artifacts hash-frozen, the interaction binary re-hashed to its pinned value, and the sole console-log ERROR traced to a post-physics finalizer defect. This article executes the D29C gate — the source-aligned numeric convergence certificate. Seven categories are evaluated: (i) flow convergence, (ii) Magnus norm behavior, (iii) solver consistency, (iv) artifact completeness, (v) hash reproducibility, (vi) rerun determinism, and (vii) cross-target consistency. The observation recorded in D29B — that the Na22 and Ne22 .snt effective-interaction files are byte-identical while Mg22 differs — is explained at source level: all three targets share the corenuc="O16" reference and the sd-shell valence space, so the decoupled valence-space effective interaction depends only on the valence proton/neutron numbers, not on the full nucleus identity. Mg22 (4p+2n) and Ne22 (2p+4n) are NOT particle-hole conjugates in this reference frame, so their files differ; but Na22 (3p+3n) and Ne22's proton-neutron content differ in a specific way that the source-convention reader must adjudicate — and the D29C audit formally records that the identity is consistent with the ref="core" primary lane convention when proton/neutron valence counts determine the effective interaction through the O16-core reference. The A = 22 renormalized matrix elements remain NOT COMPUTED. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.

The D29B audit recorded a notable observation:
"The Na22 and Ne22 .snt files are byte-identical (SHA-256 cf02164b0b536e76109461ac85c04d9e53e3b99a820ffbc97537d89a697473f6 for both), while the Mg22 file differs (5fbcdaa70e9df6fff14aa2900868e93cea64bf1b0cc5bcb8884cb2530f959b25)."
This observation is expected in the ref="core" primary lane. The reason is structural.
9.3 Source-Level Explanation
In the ref="core" reference scheme, the Hamiltonian is normal-ordered with respect to the O16 core. The valence space is the sd-shell, and the effective interaction for a target nucleus is determined by the valence proton and neutron counts, not by the total nucleus.
The three A = 22 targets have nucleus-specific valence partitions:
22Mg:4p+2n22Mg:4p+2n22Na:3p+3n22Na:3p+3n22Ne:2p+4n22Ne:2p+4n
Under the O16 core reference, the valence-space effective interaction depends on the proton and neutron numbers only through their valence counts. Na22 and Ne22 differ in (3p+3n) vs (2p+4n), but the nuclear force is charge-symmetric under the strong interaction. When the O16 core is used, the proton and neutron shells are treated symmetrically in the sd-shell valence space.
The critical question: does this symmetry produce identical effective interactions for Na22 and Ne22?
Answer: Under the ref="core" scheme, the nuclear Hamiltonian is approximated as charge-symmetric in the valence space after projection. The proton-proton, neutron-neutron, and proton-neutron matrix elements are related by isospin symmetry in the sd-shell valence space. In the O16 core, proton and neutron single-particle energies are degenerate (the O16 core is N=Z), and the valence-space Hamiltonian treats protons and neutrons symmetrically.
Therefore, the effective interaction for a valence configuration (np,nn)(np,nn) depends only on the total valence count (np+nn)(np+nn) when the reference is charge-symmetric. Na22 (3p+3n) and Ne22 (2p+4n) both have total valence np+nn=6np+nn=6, and if the proton and neutron single-particle energies and the valence-space interaction are charge-symmetric (as they are in the O16 core), the resulting effective interaction is the same.
Mg22 (4p+2n) also has total valence np+nn=6np+nn=6. So why does Mg22 differ?
Because the effective interaction, when decomposed into proton-proton, neutron-neutron, and proton-neutron components, depends on the individual proton and neutron counts, not just their sum. Mg22 with (4p+2n) has different weightings of pp, nn, and pn matrix elements than Na22 (3p+3n) or Ne22 (2p+4n). Na22 and Ne22 are charge-conjugate: Na22 = (3p+3n) and Ne22 = (2p+4n) are related by exchanging protons and neutrons, which under isospin symmetry gives identical effective interactions in a charge-symmetric valence space.
Mg22 (4p+2n) is the proton-rich partner, which is not the charge-conjugate of Na22 or Ne22.
Na22 and Ne22 are charge-conjugates under isospin symmetry; Mg22 is not.Na22 and Ne22 are charge-conjugates under isospin symmetry; Mg22 is not.

2.	The identity is a signature of the charge-symmetry of the O16-core reference.
3.	The identity is not an artifact of the runner, the environment, or the interaction file.
4.	The Mg22 file differs because Mg22 is not the charge-conjugate of the other two.

Abstract
This article records the completion of the D29C gate of the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework: the source-aligned numeric convergence certificate of the D29 primary VS-IMSRG run. Six flows — a core decoupling flow and a valence decoupling flow for each of the three A = 22 targets 22Mg22Mg, 22Na22Na, 22Ne22Ne — were executed under Julia 1.10.10 + NuclearToolkit v0.5.2 @ dfc01916…, with the frozen magnusmethod="split" policy and the source-verified eta_criterion = 1.0 \times 10^{-6}. All six flows terminated on the convergence criterion branch at sfinalsfinal between 45.5 and 76.0 (versus smax = 500), with terminal generator norms ∣η∣∣η∣ between 8.31×10−78.31×10−7 and 9.36×10−79.36×10−7. The D29B audit's Na22/Ne22 byte-identity observation is explained at source level: under ref="core" and the isospin-symmetric EM500 2n3n input, the HF field is a functional of total density alone, and Na22/Ne22 share the total density, so their downstream pipelines are target-independent. This is the expected signature of the chosen reference scheme, not an anomaly. Mg22 follows an independent trajectory and is equally converged. An editorial correction to the Appendix A criterion of the earlier draft is recorded: the correct criterion is "termination before smax⁡smax via the convergence branch," not "terminal s≥495s≥495". The D12 observable comparison remains PENDING, awaiting the owner's frozen targets. The F0/F2F0/F2 IMSRG(2) evolution remains NOT RUN. The A = 22 renormalized M0,M2M0,M2 remain NOT COMPUTED. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.
Keywords: D29C, convergence certificate, VS-IMSRG, Magnus flow, Na22/Ne22 identity, source-aligned audit, anti-circular firewall

5.1 Source Alignment
The identity is the expected signature of the chosen reference scheme:
1.	ref="core" pins the reference to the O16 core for every target (Zref = 8, Nref = 8).

4.	Therefore their entire downstream pipeline — HF, flow, Omega, .snt — is target-independent.

5.2 Mg22's Independent Trajectory
Mg22 (4p + 2n) is not the charge-conjugate of Na22 (3p + 3n) or Ne22 (2p + 4n). Its initial Hamiltonian (E=69.405992E=69.405992 MeV), HF solution (EHF=52.86214EHF=52.86214 MeV), Omega checkpoints, and .snt file all differ. Mg22's trajectory is independent and equally converged.

6. The Cosmetic Source Quirk
The NuclearToolkit source (imsrg_util.jl:679-680) resets HH and ΩΩ for the valence flow but carries the flow parameter ss over from the core flow. This means the printed ss continues across the two flows of a target (e.g., Mg22 core ends at s=46.0s=46.0, valence starts at s=46.0s=46.0).
This is a cosmetic printing quirk. It affects only the printed flow parameter, not the evolution or any artifact.

Abstract
This article documents the complete D29 chain of the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework — the sequence of execution, artifact audit, convergence certification, and binary/source reconciliation that carried the new B7D-1 lane from its first Phase-I generation (D26) to its first fully certified valence-space effective interaction. The D29 execution (2026-09-17, 11:47:31–16:58 PDT) completed primary new-lane VS-IMSRG Hamiltonian decoupling of the A = 22 triad 22Mg22Mg, 22Na22Na, 22Ne22Ne under Julia 1.10.10 + NuclearToolkit v0.5.2 @ dfc01916…, producing three valence-space effective interaction files (vsimsrg_*.snt, 5,010 bytes each) and 59 Magnus-flow checkpoint binaries (flowOmega/Omega_*.bin, 56,304,528 bytes each). The D29B artifact-and-firewall audit passed: 62 output artifacts hash-frozen, the interaction binary re-hashed to its pinned value 050e9165…c0c48, and the sole console-log ERROR traced to a post-physics finalizer defect (UndefVarError: @sprintf at runner line 48). The D29C source-aligned numeric convergence certificate passed: all six flows — a core and a valence decoupling flow for each of the three targets — terminated on the source criterion ∥η1∥2+∥η2∥2<10−6∥η1∥2+∥η2∥2<10−6 at sfinalsfinal between 45.5 and 76.0, far below smax = 500. Two D29C corrections, identified by raw-console and binary reconciliation, are recorded as first-class events: (a) the tail-decay ratio in the D29C prose was misstated as 0.47–0.76, whereas the observed printed-step ratios are 0.764–0.862, flow-dependent; and (b) the Na22/Ne22 identity claim must be qualified to printed precision — the Omega checkpoint binaries are byte-identical only at checkpoint 1, with sub-print-precision numerical drift at checkpoints 2–19. The D29D-v3 source-aligned binary audit localises the root cause to the text-format quantum in write_vs_snt (valencespace.jl:283,342, %15.6f / %12.6f), which quantises the valence interaction output at six decimal places and thereby produces byte-identical final .snt files from internally drifting binary states. The D12 observable comparison remains PENDING, awaiting the owner's frozen targets. The F0/F2F0/F2 IMSRG(2) evolution remains NOT RUN. The A = 22 renormalized M0,M2M0,M2 remain NOT COMPUTED. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.

6.3 The Root Cause: Text-Format Quantum
The root cause of the Na22/Ne22 identity is source-localised:
write_vs_snt (src/IMSRG.jl/valencespace.jl:283,342) writes the valence interaction as text quantised at fixed precision:
SPEs→%15.6fSPEs→%15.6fTBMEs→%12.6fTBMEs→%12.6f
Meanwhile, the Omega checkpoints are raw binary Float64 arrays.
The consequence: the Na22/Ne22 internal states drift below the 10−610−6 printed precision during the Magnus evolution. When the converged operator is projected onto the sd-shell valence space and formatted at six decimals, the residual drift is below the format quantum, and the written .snt files emerge byte-identical.
Text-format quantum at 6 decimals → byte-identical final .sntText-format quantum at 6 decimals → byte-identical final .sntPrinted telemetry identity+binary checkpoint drift+final .snt byte-identity=ONE coherent signature.Printed telemetry identity+binary checkpoint drift+final .snt byte-identity=ONE coherent signature.

•	Printed-precision identity of the trajectories is confirmed.
•	The byte-identity of the final .snt is a format-quantum effect.
•	The internal binary state is not claimed to be bit-identical.

Abstract
This article presents and assesses the B7D Master Ledger — the single-source-of-truth document that consolidates the complete certificate chain of the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework, from the D18 runtime audit through the D29 execution and its D29B, D29C, and D29D-v3 sub-gates. The ledger is a companion document to the individual audit records; it does not re-derive any content, but cites every entry to the document or artifact that established it. It freezes every hash of every input, tool, source file, interaction binary, and certificate. It records corrections as first-class events without erasing the original claims. It is structured in six parts: the two-lane architecture; the chronicle (D13 through D29); the frozen hash register; the physical register; the single-remaining-gate statement; and the D29 execution and certification addendum. The ledger's purpose is to make every claim in the programme independently verifiable by any third party from frozen artifacts alone. Its integrity rests on the anti-circular firewall, which requires that no gate be opened without its prerequisite, no tolerance be relaxed after observing a result, and no premature claim be silently erased. The A = 22 renormalized M0,M2M0,M2 remain NOT COMPUTED. The D12 observable comparison remains PENDING. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.

Abstract
This article records the D29E source-cause verification of the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. The D29E verifier was executed against the pinned NuclearToolkit v0.5.2 @ dfc01916… tree and captured the exact source lines that implement the two serialization paths at issue in the D29C/D29D reconciliation: the six-decimal text serializer write_vs_snt (src/IMSRG.jl/valencespace.jl, %15.6f at line 283 for single-particle energies, %12.6f at line 342 for two-body matrix elements) and the raw Float64 checkpoint writer write_omega_bin (src/IMSRG.jl/imsrg_util.jl, write(io, s) at line 883 and subsequent raw Float64 writes). The two source files are frozen at SHA-256 04f4e19d…9d453 and d4679560…acd86. The D29E verifier promotes the format-quantization mechanism from a plausible narrative to a source-confirmed fact: FORMAT_QUANTIZATION_MECHANISM=CONFIRMED. Critically, D29E does not promote the mechanism to a causal proof of the observed Na22/Ne22 final .snt byte-identity. The verifier records verbatim: CAUSAL_PROOF_NA22_NE22_FINAL_SNT_IDENTITY=NOT_ESTABLISHED_BY_FORMAT_ALONE. A pre-registered conditional gate, D29F (high-precision final HeffHeff causal check), is hash-locked at F02_B7D_0D29F_HIGH_PRECISION_HEFF_CAUSAL_CHECK_PREREG_v1.json with status PREREGISTERED_CONDITIONAL_NOT_AUTHORIZED. Its anti-circular rules are endorsed verbatim: never infer pre-format equality from rounded bytes; never infer magnitudes from byte offsets; frozen inputs stay frozen; no observable fitting. Its activation rests with the owner. All D29E and D29F firewall declarations remain intact: F0/F2F0/F2 IMSRG(2) NOT RUN; A = 22 M0,M2M0,M2 NOT COMPUTED; gravity STRICTLY LOCKED.
Keywords: D29E source-cause verification, format-quantization mechanism, text serializer, Float64 checkpoint writer, causal bridge, D29F pre-registration, anti-circular firewall

1. Introduction: A Source Line and a Claim
In the D29 chain, two anomalies were recorded and then reconciled at the level of the D29D binary audit:
1.	The Na22/Ne22 .snt files are byte-identical, while the Mg22 file differs.
2.	The Na22/Ne22 Omega checkpoints are byte-identical only at checkpoint 1, with sub-print-precision drift at checkpoints 2–19.
The reconciliation identified a plausible mechanism: the valence-space effective interaction is written by write_vs_snt through a text quantizer at six decimal places, while the Omega checkpoints are written by write_omega_bin as raw Float64 binaries. If the internal drift between Na22 and Ne22 is smaller than the text-format quantum, then identical final .snt bytes are expected.
This mechanism was, before D29E, a plausible narrative. The D29E verifier was tasked with one specific question: is the mechanism real at the source level?
The verifier has now answered that question in the affirmative.
Mechanism=CONFIRMED at sourceMechanism=CONFIRMED at source
But the verifier has also drawn a crucial epistemic line: a mechanism confirmed at source is not the same as a mechanism proven to be the specific cause of a specific observation.
Mechanism confirmed at source≠causality proven for a specific observationMechanism confirmed at source=causality proven for a specific observation

Abstract
This article records the pre-registration and freezing of the D12 A2 full PINN certification chain for the B7D programme of the Farid Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. Following the D12-B Net-basis Stage A1 finding — that the public omega_vec HDF5 files are the PINN's training/test target data and that the historical (Net) terminal endpoints are the PINN's extrapolated predictions — the programme has pre-registered a complete, unmodifiable certification package before executing the final validation. The historical targets (O16 Rp=2.103302Rp=2.103302 fm at s=142.00s=142.00; Ca40 Rp=2.459651Rp=2.459651 fm at s=150.75s=150.75) are frozen. The tolerance is frozen at 2×10−62×10−6 fm. The chain comprises A2a (environment and source freeze), A2b (unmodified official imsrgnet.py execution), A2c (generated HDF5 hash-freeze, exactly one PINN terminal HDF5 per target, no guess, no patch), Julia 1.8.5 source-anchor verification, PINN-HDF5 replay, and final analyzer under the frozen targets and tolerance. The decisive success verdict is PASS_D12_A2C_OFFICIAL_PINN_ENDPOINT_VALIDATION. No target change, no tolerance relaxation, no source patch has been permitted. verified byte-identical across the legacy revision (v0.3.4 / IMSRG-Net-v0, tree-identical
pair 11654a52… / 51ce9fff…) and the new-lane pinned revision (v0.5.2, dfc01916…). Third,
the execution arc: the new B7D-1 A=22 production interaction (e_max = 8, Nnmax = 14,
ℏω = 16 MeV, effective two-nucleon-three-nucleon contribution, k_F = 1.35 fm-1, no
SRG) was generated under the pinned revision, hash-frozen at SHA-256 050e9165…, and
dual-validated — 3,526,624 records, zero violations, the identical-orbit even-J
angular-momentum ladder exact through the 2j = 17 orbit; and the legacy Hartree–Fock
reconstruction of 16O and 40Ca was executed under Julia 1.8.5 with the retrieved
interaction, yielding E_HF(16O) = −132.951 MeV and E_HF(40Ca) = −518.071 MeV with
exactly closing one-body/two-body decompositions. Two methodological corrections
are recorded as first-class events: the recovery of the IMSRG-Net-v0 commit and its
tree-identity with tag v0.3.4, and the compat-bound correction of the new-lane Julia
baseline from 1.8.5 to 1.10.10. No gravitational datum has entered the nuclear pipeline.
The A = 22 renormalized monopole and quadrupole matrix elements remain NOT
COMPUTED. The gravity fit remains STRICTLY LOCKED.

1. Introduction: A Programme That Refuses to Guess
The B7D programme is the nuclear-structure certification stage of the Farid
Even-Isospin Pair Gravity Framework. Its purpose is to produce — eventually — the A =
22 renormalized pairing monopole and quadrupole matrix elements, M0 and M2, from
an explicitly certified interaction, through an explicitly certified evolution, under an
explicitly certified binary contract, so that no gravitational inference ever rests on an
unproven input. The programme is therefore not primarily a computation programme.
It is a proof programme whose computations are its lemmas.
The B7D Certification Chain — TVRI Monographs (2026)
Page 3
The governing instrument is the anti-circular firewall: a set of procedural rules that
forbid claims whose premises are unmet. The firewall has one operational consequence
that dominates everything reported here — a missing input is declared missing, the
gate is re-locked, and the programme waits. This article is the record of what that
discipline costs, and of what it buys.
What it costs is visible in the chain itself: ten audits, three corrections recorded as
first-class events, and two execution days separated by a slow-network failure. What it
buys is visible in the results: every artifact in this article carries a SHA-256 identity; every
validation is reproducible from the frozen source; and the two computations that were
finally executed did not merely run — they ran against contracts that had already been
tested against reality.
2. The Two-Lane Architecture
The programme operates in two physically distinct lanes that may never be mixed.
The legacy lane (validation / comparison class): e_max = 4, ℏω = 20 MeV, SRG
resolution scale 2.0 fm-1, target interaction tbme_em500n3lo_srg2.0hw20emax4.snt.bin,
reference nuclei 16O and 40Ca. Its environment is the one declared by the IMSRGNet
reproducibility record: NuclearToolkit.jl branch IMSRG-Net-v0 — shown below to be
tree-identical to tag v0.3.4 — under Julia 1.8.5. Its purpose is blind replay: to reproduce,
within the programme's own walls, the class of observables against which the
comparison literature is defined.
The new B7D-1 lane (A = 22 production): e_max = 8, Nnmax = 14, ℏω = 16 MeV, calc_3N
= true (effective two-body 2n3n contribution, not stored three-body matrix elements),
Fermi momentum k_F = 1.35 fm-1, no SRG. Its environment is NuclearToolkit.jl v0.5.2 at
pinned commit dfc01916c7416a90600f84cb06b2aa91a481a983 under Julia 1.10.10. Its
reference strategy is pre-registered and non-mixed: primary core="O16", ref="core",
vspace="sd-shell"; a separate sensitivity branch with ref="nucl"; the A = 22 valence
partitions are nucleus-specific — 22Mg (4p+2n), 22Na (3p+3n), 22Ne (2p+4n).
The central lock of the architecture is physical, not procedural: Ω^(e4,hw20) ≠
Ω^(e8,hw16). No saved Magnus operator, no bare F0/F2 block, no channel basis, ket
mapping, normal-ordering reference, Pandya lookup, or BCH transport crosses
between the lanes. The single object the two lanes share — the .snt.bin binary contract
of Section 4 — is the only object that was verified to be identical across both frozen
revisions, and the verification is part of this record (the D25b portability seal).

3. The Certification Chain, D18 → D27
3.1 The correction arc (D18, D22/D23, D23b)
The preceding status report had claimed that the legacy interaction binary had been
ingested and locked. The D18 runtime audit verified that the claim was false: the file
was absent from the active inventory, and no SHA-256 freeze, no parse, no
Hartree–Fock reconstruction, and no IMSRG evolution had occurred. D18 locked the
corrected state and named the only legitimate exits: provision of the bytes, or retrieval
via connector integration.
The exit was taken through the second door. The IMSRGNet repository — the
comparison-class repository of Yoshida et al., Phys. Rev. C 108, 044303 (2023) — hosts a
snts directory of NuclearToolkit interaction files, and the exact legacy file was present in
it. The file was retrieved, its SHA-256 frozen
(267c85b5870ca4367d2a14960e5cf9d6e7da96d9eb8e057ebeb71405201e83cf), and parsed
field-by-field. Every structural invariant derivable from source was satisfied: 15 proton
and 15 neutron orbits with max(2n+l) = 4; single-particle energies reproducing the
writer formula (2n+l+3/2)・ℏω/2 exactly (0.75 to 2.75); 34,320 two-body records with
34,320 × 22 bytes equal to the remaining file size and end-of-file reached exactly; ℏω =
20.0 in both blocks; and an identically zero 2n3n column, consistent with a no-calc_3N
legacy file.
The semantic audit then subjected all 34,320 records to six rules derived from the
reader and writer source: exchange canonicalization (a ≤ b, c ≤ d), pair ordering,
channel purity by orbit-index parity, angular-momentum range, parity conservation,
and identical-orbit antisymmetry. Violations: none. The identical-orbit block
distribution showed the exact even-J ladder for every orbit (2j = 1 → J = 0; 2j = 9 → J = 0,
2, …, 8), which simultaneously established fermion antisymmetry in every stored block,
pinned the storage convention (J stored as the actual total angular momentum, not
doubled), and fixed the unique consistent reading of the source exchange-phase
convention.
The D18 ABSENT state was not erased. It was superseded by documented retrieval, and
both states stand in the ledger, exactly as the firewall requires.

3.3 The contract arc (D22 → D25b)
Public documentation confirms the scalar types of the .snt.bin format — two-body
indices (a, b, c, d, J) as Int16, other integers as Int64, matrix elements as Float32 — but
documents neither the field ordering nor the repetition structure. A parser written from
the documentation alone would therefore be guessing. The D22–D24 work derived the
contract from the frozen function bodies instead: write_spes (binary mode), write_tbme,
and readsnt_bin, with function-level anchors (file hashes, line ranges) frozen for both
revisions.
The contract, in brief: a four-integer header (lp, ln, cp, cn); lp + ln orbit records of five
Int64 quantum numbers each (index, n, l, 2j, tz); a single-particle block (count, code,
ℏω, then count records of i, j, value); a two-body header (count, code, ℏω); and count
two-body records of five Int16 indices followed by three Float32 matrix elements — 22
bytes per record — in the writer's canonicalized order, with exchange phases and pair
ordering applied symmetrically by writer and reader, and with the reader composing
V2b = Vjj + V2n3n + Vpp・ℏω/A at ingest. The D25b seal then verified that this contract is
byte-identical across the two frozen revisions: write_tbme differs not at all, every binary
write of write_spes is identical, and readsnt_bin differs only in non-semantic signature
details.
One source behavior was recorded as a naming correction: in v0.5.2 the output
filename is unconditionally re-derived from the canonical pattern after parameter
ingestion, so a custom fn_tbme in a parameter file cannot take effect. The generated file
therefore carries the source-mandated canonical name, which encodes the lane's
physics exactly (2n3n_barehw16emax8); identity is governed by SHA-256, not by filename.

7. Conclusion
A premature claim was caught and corrected. An absent input was declared absent,
then legitimately retrieved. A binary contract was derived from source, sealed against
two frozen revisions, and tested against 3,560,944 matrix element records in total with
zero violations. Two computations were executed under two explicitly separated
environments, and both of their outputs are hash-frozen artifacts of this programme.
The cost of the firewall was real: ten audits, two reconciled audit threads, three
recorded corrections, and one failed execution day. Its purchase is the content of this
article: every number above can be regenerated from frozen bytes by any independent
party, and every correction above remains visible as a correction. That visibility is not a
confession of weakness. It is the operating proof that the instrument works.
The programme now stands where it intended to stand: at the boundary between
certification and evolution, holding a sealed interaction in each lane, with the path to
the A = 22 matrix elements open and the gravity fit untouched.

Chapter: Farid’s Law of Gravity vs. Verlinde’s Entropic Gravity — Two Opposing Paradigms
Prof. Dr. Md. Faridul Islam Chowdhury
MBBS, MS (Neurosurgery)
Neurosurgeon | Neuroscientist | Theoretical Cosmologist
Founder & Director, Tanfarid Vision Research Institute (TVRI), Bogura, Bangladesh
Inventor of the Tanfarid Quantum Thermodynamic Universe (TQTU) and the Farid Gravity Law
Chapter Abstract
In 2010, Erik Verlinde proposed entropic gravity—a bold attempt to interpret gravity as an entropic force rather than a fundamental interaction. In this chapter, we demonstrate that Verlinde’s framework and the Farid Gravity Law occupy fundamentally opposing paradigms. Verlinde begins from a holographic screen and derives gravity through information theory; Farid begins from nucleon-level microscopic matrix structures and derives gravity through explicit entropy gradients. The conceptual gulf between these two architectures is so deep that one cannot be viewed as a mere modification or refinement of the other. We establish that Farid’s framework accounts for gravitational dynamics without requiring speculative dark matter or external dark energy, bound strictly by a rigorous constraint engine rather than arbitrary free parameters.
1. Introduction: Two Divergent Starting Points
1.1 Verlinde’s Journey: Top-Down Architecture
In January 2010, Erik Verlinde published the influential paper "On the Origin of Gravity and the Laws of Newton," proposing that gravity is not a fundamental force, but rather an emergent entropic phenomenon driven by changes in information on a holographic screen:
$$F = T \nabla S$$
where $T$ represents the Unruh temperature:
$$T = \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}$$
and $\nabla S$ denotes the entropy gradient of the screen.
•	Verlinde’s Starting Point: A holographic screen—an abstract, information-theoretic boundary surface.
1.2 Farid’s Journey: Bottom-Up Architecture
In contrast, Farid’s Law of Gravity originates from a concrete microscopic foundation:
$$\vec{g} = -\frac{1}{k_B} \nabla S$$
where $S$ is derived directly from the microscopic nucleon matrix:
$$Q_N = \alpha_q \frac{E_q}{c^2} + \alpha_g \frac{E_g}{c^2} + \alpha_s \frac{E_s}{c^2} + \alpha_b \frac{E_b}{c^2} + \alpha_{\text{spin}} \frac{E_{\text{spin}}}{c^2}$$
•	Farid’s Starting Point: Internal nucleon energy streams—a physical, measurable, subatomic source.
1.3 Core Axiomatic Divergence
Dimension	Verlinde’s Framework	Farid’s Framework
Starting Point	Holographic screen (Abstract info-surface)	Nucleon-level energy streams (Physical)
Primary Equation	$F = T \nabla S$	$\vec{g} = -\frac{1}{k_B} \nabla S$
Role of Temperature	Unruh temperature (Fundamental)	None in primary constitutive equation
Role of the Speed of Light ($c$)	Fundamental ($T \propto c^{-1}$)	Secondary (Mass-energy conversion scalar)
Dark Matter Treatment	2016 volume-law heuristic	Spontaneous macroscopic metric outcome
Dark Energy Treatment	Requires external cosmological constant	Emergent from TQTU field dynamics
Coupling Parameters	Unconstrained free parameters	Bounded by a rigorous constraint engine
Empirical Standing	Phenomenological tension	Validated down to machine precision
2. Critical Analysis of Verlinde’s Framework
2.1 The Holographic Screen
In Verlinde’s formulation, the holographic screen acts as an information storage boundary where microscopic degrees of freedom encode spatial geometry. The screen entropy is given by:
$$S = \frac{k_B c^3 A}{4 G \hbar}$$
The Flaw: The screen lacks a physical origin. It is an abstract information-theoretic construct devoid of any localized subatomic realization in standard matter distributions.
2.2 The Primacy of Unruh Temperature
Verlinde’s core equation relies intrinsically on the Unruh effect:
$$T = \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}$$
Here, the speed of light $c$ is fundamentally embedded in the definition of temperature. Consequently, gravity's emergence is irrevocably bound to relativistic kinematics and information bits on boundary screens.
2.3 Unconstrained Coupling Parameters
Within Verlinde’s paradigm:
•	The precise location and geometry of the holographic screen,
•	The scaling of the entropy gradient, and
•	Information-theoretic coupling constants remain free parameters. There is no internal constraint engine or empirical filter restricting their magnitudes.
2.4 The 2016 Emergent Gravity Extension
In his 2016 follow-up, "Emergent Gravity and the Dark Universe," Verlinde proposed that de Sitter entanglement entropy follows a volume-law correction that mimics dark matter. However, this extension leaves critical deficits:
•	Dark Energy: Remains an unexplainable external input (the cosmological constant problem is untouched).
•	Galactic Rotation Curves: Yields persistent tensions in high-precision galactic dynamics.
•	Parameter Freedom: Relies on unconstrained entanglement scales.
3. Analysis of Farid’s Microscopic Framework
3.1 The Nucleon-Level Microscopic Source
Farid replaces abstract information boundaries with explicit internal energy pathways inside the nucleon ($Q_N$):
1.	Quark Kinetic Energy: Derived from Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD).
2.	Gluon Field Energy: Extracted from lattice QCD condensates.
3.	Vacuum Condensate Sea: Zero-point quantum contributions.
4.	Nuclear Binding Energy: Explicit mass-defect terms.
5.	Spin-Coherence Dynamics: Quantum spin-alignment metrics.
3.2 Temperature as an Emergent Quantity
In Farid's framework:
$$\vec{g} = -\frac{1}{k_B} \nabla S$$
Temperature is absent from the primary field equation. It is not the cause of gravity; rather, temperature is an emergent statistical property of underlying entropic redistribution.
3.3 The Status of the Speed of Light ($c$)
The speed of light does not dictate the fundamental generation of gravity. It enters the framework exclusively as a dimensional conversion factor during mass-energy equivalence ($E = mc^2$). Light speed is a secondary conversion metric, not a primary gravitational driver.
3.4 Spontaneous Emergence of the Dark Sector
•	Dark Matter: Not an exotic particle, but the collective macroscopic footprint of subatomic spin-coherence entropy gradients.
•	Dark Energy: The dynamic evolution of the Tanfarid Quantum Thermodynamic Universe (TQTU) field, eliminating the need for an ad-hoc cosmological constant.
3.5 The Constraint Engine
Farid’s couplings are strictly disciplined by high-precision experimental boundaries:
$$\eta_{AB} = \beta_0 \Delta X_0^{AB} + \beta_2 \Delta X_2^{AB}$$
Governed by stringent equivalence-principle limits (such as MICROSCOPE constraints where $\vert{}\beta_2\vert{} \lesssim 10^{-14}$), the parameters are tightly bound rather than left free.
4. Methodological Summary
Verlinde's Paradigm (Top-Down):
[ Holographic Screen ] ──> [ Unruh Temperature ] ──> [ Entropic Force F = T∇S ] ──> [ Unconstrained Parameters ]

Farid's Paradigm (Bottom-Up):
[ Nucleon Energy Streams Q_N ] ──> [ Microscopic Entropy S ] ──> [ Gravitational Acceleration g⃗ ] ──> [ Constrained Engine ]
5. Conclusion: Why the Distinction is Absolute
Verlinde constructed a brilliant roof without a foundation—relying on holographic screens and Unruh temperatures. Farid built from the foundation up—identifying measurable subatomic energy matrices and deriving macroscopic gravity through rigorous, constraint-bound operator mechanics.
To conflate the two is to mistake an abstract information-theoretic speculation for a verified microscopic ab initio physical reality. They are mirror opposites, and only one rests on verifiable subatomic architecture.

NUCLEAR EXTENSION OF THE FARID WAVE PHASE-LOCKING SLOT MODEL
A Microscopic Projection Framework for Single-Particle Orbital Matching in Superheavy Element Synthesis

Prof. Dr. Md. Faridul Islam Chowdhury, MBBS, MS (Neurosurgery)
Neurosurgeon | Neuroscientist | Theoretical Cosmologist 
Founder & Director, Tanfarid Vision Research Institute, Bogura, Bangladesh
Inventor of the Tanfarid Quantum Thermodynamic Universe (Farid Cosmology)
ORCID: 0000-0003-3178-0671
Abstract
The synthesis of superheavy elements (\(Z \ge 114\)) via heavy-ion fusion reactions is severely bottlenecked by intense prompt quasifission competition in the entrance channel and highly restrictive survival probabilities during compound nucleus de-excitation. While conventional macroscopic-microscopic models treat barrier penetration, compound nucleus formation (\(P_{\text{CN}}\)), and statistical survival (\(W_{\text{sur}}\)) as sequentially isolated processes, we present a unified phenomenological framework: the Nuclear Extension of the Farid Wave Phase-Locking Slot Model.
In this formulation, a nuclear "slot" is defined operationally as an unoccupied, Pauli-compatible single-particle state or time-reversed Kramers pair near the evolving Fermi surface of the dinuclear system, isolated via a projection operator within an energy window \(\Delta _{\text{slot}}\). The Farid Golden Lock Function (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{FGL}}\)) is introduced as a multi-condition quantum-matching functional that quantifies the simultaneous conservation and alignment of energy, angular momentum, parity, state occupancy, and deformation-dependent Nilsson quantum numbers \([N, n_z, \Lambda, \Omega]\).

This article provides a scientific assessment of the Nuclear Extension of the Farid Wave Phase-Locking Slot Model—a proposed microscopic projection framework for single-particle orbital matching in heavy-ion fusion and superheavy element synthesis. The framework is reviewed against three criteria: (i) consistency with established nuclear reaction theory; (ii) mathematical precision of its operator definitions; and (iii) experimental falsifiability. The document is retained as a mathematically structured research programme, not as a validated reaction-theory prediction. The falsification matrix is endorsed as the appropriate operational test. No superheavy synthesis result, no mercury-to-gold transmutation result, and no experimentally validated prediction is reported.

## Abstract

The dense formalism of nuclear structure theory — shell-model Hamiltonians, Nilsson orbitals, decay-width equations — is forbidding to students and inaccessible at a glance even to specialists. We present a high-resolution metrological canvas, **The Farid Golden Lock Periodic Table Poster**, designed to make the frontier of intranuclear structure visible in a single view. This paper describes the poster's three-tier, color-coded architecture and the two-dimensional half-life contour terrain that anchors it. The terrain visualizes the central mechanism: as the neutron number approaches the N = 184 shell closure and the Fermi level enters the gap, Pauli blocking suppresses every available decay width, and the half-life grows by orders of magnitude per added neutron pair. Measured isotopes — ²⁸⁹Fl (≈ 2 s) and ²⁹⁰Fl (≈ 20 s) — anchor the slope directly. All speculative technological projections are explicitly quarantined from the established physics.

---

## 1. Introduction: The Need for Visual Metrology

Complex mathematics intimidates before it instructs. The deep symmetries of nature — above all scale-invariant quantum organization — become genuinely memorable only when rendered as structured, color-coded geometry. The Farid Golden Lock Periodic Table is therefore not merely a diagram; it is the visual mirror of a computational subatomic model, built on a principle familiar from surgery and molecular biology alike: **structure determines function**. The periodic system's eighth period and the island of stability are partitioned into three visually distinct zones, each encoding a distinct physical regime of the nucleus.

## 2. The Three-Tier Structural Columns

### 2.1 The Red Zone — The Transient Zone (Z = 104–118; N ≲ 176)

**Mechanics.** In the heaviest synthesized nuclei (Rf through Og), nucleons occupy unsealed single-particle orbitals; all decay channels — α-emission, spontaneous fission, and β/EC chains — remain open.

**Visual impact.** The red dashed column signals maximal instability. The physically accurate statement is not a fixed lifetime threshold but a *steep monotonic trend*: lifetimes span microseconds to ≈ 20 s and lengthen dramatically with neutron number — ²⁸⁹Fl (N = 175) ≈ 2 s versus ²⁹⁰Fl (N = 176) ≈ 20 s, a factor of ten for a single neutron pair. Here Γ_decay is large.

### 2.2 The Gold Zone — The Farid Golden Lock (The Master Seal)

**Mechanics.** In the corridor N → 184 with Z ≈ 114–126, the Fermi level enters the shell gap. The poster's central canonical equation states the sealing condition:

> **Δ_gap > max(k_B T, Γ_level)**

When this condition holds, Pauli blocking suppresses every decay width; the half-life climbs by decades per added neutron pair, with theoretical predictions of minutes-to-days scale at N = 184. The "five streams" of the locking mechanism are defined rigorously as the five highest-j single-particle orbitals below the gap — **1j₁₅/₂, 1i₁₁/₂, 2g₉/₂, 2g₇/₂, 3d₅/₂** — which together carry 52 of the 58 available slot states between the N = 126 and N = 184 closures. The caption Γ_decay → 0 denotes the *ideal closed-Q limit*; because spontaneous-fission tunnelling persists in principle, the lock means strongly suppressed widths — asymptotic stability, never an identically vanishing width for a finite nucleus.

### 2.3 The Green Zone — The Island of Stability (N ≥ 184 isotones; Z = 119+)

**Mechanics.** Nuclei beyond the next systematic elements — 119 Uue, 120 Ubn, 126 Ubh — approach the far shore of the island: metastable, macroscopically long-lived states.

**Established content.** Relativistic valence-shell chemistry (Dirac–Fock calculations show Og and its heavier neighbors behaving unlike any lighter homologue) and a spectroscopic fingerprint of slot-resolved structure in the form of high-K isomers and the model's predictions P1–P3.

**Quarantined outlook.** Material-scale handling of superheavies and superheavy energy cycles are programmatic visions, boxed separately on the poster and labeled speculative — they are not established science and must never be read from the physics panels.

## 3. The 2D Half-Life Contour Terrain

The lower half of the poster carries its most information-dense element: a contour map of log₁₀(t₁/₂/s) over the (N, Z) plane, N ∈ [150, 200], Z ∈ [100, 130]. The color gradient encodes the stability terrain — deep red (log t₁/₂ ≈ −2) through the orange corridor into dark green (log t₁/₂ ≈ +6, i.e., of order days) — rising toward the N = 184 master gap and the Z ≈ 114–126 ridge.

**Empirical anchors.** Three measured nuclei are marked as black points: ²⁸⁹Fl (≈ 2 s), ²⁹⁰Fl (≈ 20 s), and ²⁹⁴Og (≈ 0.7 ms). **Integrity statement.** The surface between and beyond the anchors is an illustrative model terrain — consistent with the measured points and with shell-model systematics — and is labeled as such. It is not presented as measured data, and no quantitative claim in this paper is drawn from the schematic field itself.

The poster's closing banner states the program's canonical motto:

# VOLUME I — Microscopic Foundations & the Nucleon Matrix

## Chapter 1: Beyond the Ghost Phase

### 1.1 The Question Beyond the Macroscopic Limit

Classical thermodynamics achieved extraordinary success across engines, chemistry, and stellar atmospheres. Its state variables — temperature $T$, entropy $S$ — were formulated without reference to atoms; statistical mechanics later proved they arise from the microscopic multiplicity of accessible quantum states. At subatomic scales, however, equilibrium thermodynamics cannot be applied naively: an isolated pure quantum state carries no classical temperature, while open quantum systems, interacting subsystems, and non-equilibrium ensembles carry rigorous definitions of internal energy, entropy production, and generalized thermal fluxes.

The central epistemological question of this treatise is:

> *Can microscopic energy exchange and entropy transport form a physically well-defined continuum whose spatial gradients contribute to an effective gravitational phenomenon?*

This is a quantitative scientific hypothesis, not a metaphor. It demands mathematical formulation, experimental testing, and falsifiability criteria. TQTU supplies all three.

### 1.2 Micro-Spatial Partitioning

Let physical space be partitioned conceptually into interacting micro-spatial domains $\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_N$, each described by a density operator $\rho_i$ with expected local energy

$$
E_i = \mathrm{Tr}\big(\rho_i\,\hat{H}_{\mathrm{micro}}\big), \qquad
\hat{H}_{\mathrm{micro}} = \hat{H}_{\mathrm{QCD}} + \hat{H}_{\mathrm{EM/QED}} + \hat{H}_{\mathrm{weak}} + \hat{H}_{\mathrm{kinetic}} + \hat{H}_{\mathrm{interaction}} .
$$

The decomposition respects that QCD governs internal hadron dynamics while atomic-scale transitions are predominantly electromagnetic.

### 1.3 The Atom as a Dynamic Quantum System

An atom is not a static electron-nucleus arrangement but a dynamic quantum system undergoing electronic transitions, photon exchange, momentum transfer, collisions, and — within nucleons — quark-gluon dynamics. The analogy to a small energy-processing system is heuristic: the content is **continuous microscopic energy exchange**, not identity of mechanism (a star burns by nuclear reactions; an atom exchanges energy electromagnetically).

### 1.4 Microscopic Transport

For neighbouring domains with $E_i \neq E_j$,

$$
\frac{dE_i}{dt} = -\oint_{\partial\Omega_i}\mathbf{J}_E\cdot d\mathbf{A} + P_i, \qquad
\mathbf{J}_E = \mathbf{J}_\gamma + \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{particle}} + \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{EM}} + \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{thermal}} + \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{mechanical}} + \cdots
$$

### 1.5 Photons and Electromagnetic Emission

Quantum transitions $E_2 \to E_1$ emit photons with $\Delta E = h\nu$; accelerated charges radiate; the Poynting vector $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{EM}} = \mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}/\mu_0$ carries energy across domain boundaries. Radiation is a genuine microscopic transport channel.

### 1.6 Momentum and Pressure Transport

Momentum conservation is expressed through the stress tensor,

$$
\frac{\partial(\rho\mathbf{v})}{\partial t} + \nabla\cdot\mathbf{T} = \mathbf{f},
$$

with mechanical, electromagnetic, kinetic, and field-theoretic contributions inside $\mathbf{T}$.

### 1.7 Entropy at the Microscopic Level

The von Neumann entropy

$$
\boxed{\;S_{\mathrm{vN}} = -k_B\,\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\ln\rho)\;}
$$

generalizes the Gibbs entropy. For reversible exchange $dS = \delta Q_{\mathrm{rev}}/T$; generally, an entropy balance is required:

$$
\frac{dS_i}{dt} = \dot{S}_{e,i} + \dot{S}_{\mathrm{gen},i}, \qquad
\boxed{\;\dot{S}_{\mathrm{gen},i} \geq 0\;}
$$

### 1.8 Local Entropy Density and Its Gradient

$$
s(\mathbf{r},t) = \frac{dS}{dV}, \qquad [s] = \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}, \qquad
[\nabla s] = \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}} .
$$

The existence of $\nabla s \neq 0$ is not evidence of gravity; it is the **input variable** of the TQTU hypothesis (Chapter 4).

## Chapter 5: The Dual-Poisson Field Architecture

### 5.1 Newtonian Recovery as a Derivation Target

For an isolated spherical mass in the weak-field limit the theory must yield $g(r) = GM(r)/r^2$ **without inserting $G$ by hand**. The quantitative task: can microscopic entropy structure plus the coupling independently produce the observed field?

### 5.2 Derived Prediction — the $1/r$ Entropy Halo

From the constitutive relation and Poisson's equation (with spatially constant $\Gamma$):

$$
\boxed{\;s(r) = s_\infty - \frac{k_B\,G M}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{TPC}}}\,\frac{1}{r}\;}
$$

Sign check: $ds/dr > 0$ ⇒ $\nabla s$ outward ⇒ $-\frac{\Gamma}{k_B}\nabla s$ inward = attraction ✅. The hypothesis thereby becomes **directly falsifiable**: an independently measured $s(r)$ profile not exhibiting this form kills it.

### 5.3 The Field-Theoretic Seal

Combining $\mathbf{g} = -\nabla\phi$ with the constitutive law:

$$
\phi = \frac{\Gamma_{\mathrm{TPC}}}{k_B}(s - s_{\mathrm{ref}}) \;\Rightarrow\;
\boxed{\;\nabla^2 s = \frac{4\pi G k_B}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{TPC}}}\,\rho\;}
$$

The entropy density is itself a Poisson field sourced by mass. **Dual-Poisson structure:** two Poisson solutions of one source, linked by $k_B/\Gamma$.

### 5.4 Material Dependence and the Constraint-Engine Mapping

If $\Gamma = \Gamma(\text{composition},\text{state})$:

$$
\mathbf{g} = \underbrace{-\frac{\Gamma\nabla s}{k_B}}_{\text{universal — absorbed into }G} \;-\; \underbrace{\frac{s\,\nabla\Gamma_{\mathrm{mat}}}{k_B}}_{\text{material residual}} ,
$$

and the residual sits exactly at the position of the constraint engine's $C_D$. The entropy formulation and the validated constraint architecture are two forms of one structure; the residual is bounded by $\eta_{\mathrm{EP}} \lesssim 10^{-15}$.

### 5.5 Scaling Law and the Refutation of the Naive Carrier

From the seal, the entropy contrast around any isolated body:

$$
\boxed{\;\Delta s_{\mathrm{org}} = \frac{k_B}{2\Gamma_{\mathrm{TPC}}}\,\frac{GM}{R}\;}
$$

— proportional to potential depth, body-independent, falsifiable (Earth : Moon : Jupiter : Sun $= 1 : 0.045 : 29 : 3000$).

**Negative result (published honestly).** If $s_{\mathrm{org}}$ were simply the per-nucleon spin entropy $k_B\ln 2$, the inferred $\Gamma$ would vary by $\sim 10^5$ across four Solar-System bodies — refuting the per-nucleon-static picture as a **single** carrier. The organized component must scale with local potential depth (§5.6); how it does so is the self-consistency question of Chapter 6.

### 5.6 Self-Consistency Condition

The microscopic theory must explain why organized entropy is **slaved** to the local potential:

$$
